title.zh: 卷三百四十一 列傳第一百 王存 孫固 趙瞻 傅堯俞
title.en: Volume 341 Biographies 100: Wang Cun, Sun Gu, Zhao Zhan, Fu Yao Yu
title.raw: 卷三百四十一 列傳第一百 王存 孫固 趙瞻 傅堯俞 Volume 341 Biographies 100: Wang Cun, Sun Gu, Zhao Zhan, Fu Yao Yu

sentences.zh: 王存 孫固 趙瞻 傅堯俞

translations.literal: Wang Cun, Sun Gu, Zhao Zhan, Fu Yaoyu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cun, Sun Gu, Zhao Zhan, and Fu Yaoyu

sentences.zh: 王存，字正仲，潤州丹陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Cun, style name Zhengzhong, was a man of Danyang in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cun, whose style name was Zhengzhong, was a native of Danyang in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼善讀書，年十二，辭親從師於江西，五年始歸。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at reading; at age twelve he left his parents to follow a teacher in Jiangxi, and only after five years did he return.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was adept at reading; at twelve he left his family to study under a teacher in Jiangxi and did not return for five years.

sentences.zh: 時學者方尚雕篆，獨為古文數十篇，鄉老先生見之，自以為不及。

translations.literal: At the time scholars were esteeming ornate carving and inlay; he alone composed several tens of pieces in the ancient style, and when the village elders saw them they considered themselves not his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of the day prized florid, ornamental composition; he alone drafted several dozen pieces in the antiquated style, and when the village elders saw them they judged themselves his inferior.

sentences.zh: 慶歷六年，登進士第，調嘉興主簿，擢上虞令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingli he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed to Jiaxing as registrar, and was promoted to magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qingli (1046) he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed recorder in Jiaxing, and was promoted to magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 豪姓殺人，久莫敢問，存至，按以州吏受賕，豪賂他官變其獄，存反為罷去。

translations.literal: A powerful surname had committed murder, and for long none dared inquire; when Cun arrived he investigated and found a prefectural clerk had taken bribes, the powerful clan bribed other officials to alter the case, and Cun was instead dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful clan had committed murder, and for a long time no one dared investigate. When Cun arrived he pursued the case and found that a prefectural clerk had taken bribes; the powerful family bribed other officials to reverse the verdict, and Cun was dismissed instead.

sentences.zh: 久之，除密州推官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed reviewing official in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed judicial reviewer in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 修潔自重，為歐陽修、呂公著、趙概所知。

translations.literal: Cultivated in purity and holding himself in restraint, he came to the knowledge of Ouyang Xiu, Lü Gongzhu, and Zhao Gai.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivated in purity and self-restraint, he came to the notice of Ouyang Xiu, Lü Gongzhu, and Zhao Gai.

sentences.zh: 治平中，入為國子監直講，遷秘書省著作佐郎，歷館閣校勘、集賢校理、史館檢討、知太常禮院。

translations.literal: During Zhiping he entered service as direct lecturer at the Directorate of Education, was promoted to assistant compiler in the Secretariat, and successively served as collator in the palace libraries, collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents, examiner in the History Office, and overseer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era he entered service as direct lecturer at the Imperial University, was promoted to assistant compiler in the Secretariat, and successively served as collator in the palace libraries, collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents, examiner in the History Office, and director of rites at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 存故與王安石厚，安石執政，數引與論事，不合，即謝不往。

translations.literal: Cun had formerly been thick with Wang Anshi; when Anshi held power he repeatedly summoned him to discuss affairs, but when they did not agree he excused himself and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Cun had once been on close terms with Wang Anshi; when Anshi took power he repeatedly summoned Cun to discuss policy, but when they disagreed Cun excused himself and ceased to attend.

sentences.zh: 存在三館歷年，不少貶以干進。

translations.literal: During his years in the Three Institutes he never in the least lowered himself to advance his career.
translations.idiomatic: During his years in the Three Institutes he never lowered himself in the least to advance his career.

sentences.zh: 嘗召見便殿，累上書陳時政，因及大臣，無所附麗，皆時人難言者。

translations.literal: He was once summoned to the informal palace hall and repeatedly submitted memorials on current affairs, touching even great ministers, without attaching himself anywhere—all matters others found hard to speak.
translations.idiomatic: He was once summoned to the informal palace hall and repeatedly submitted memorials on current affairs, including matters touching great ministers, without attaching himself to any faction—topics others found hard to speak.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，神宗察其忠實無黨，以為國史編修官、修起居注。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng Emperor Shenzong perceived his loyalty and lack of faction and appointed him compiler of the national history and recorder of imperial actions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanfeng (1078) Emperor Shenzong perceived his loyalty and lack of faction and appointed him compiler of the national history and recorder of imperial actions.

sentences.zh: 時起居注雖日侍，而奏事必稟中書俟旨。

translations.literal: At the time, though the recorder of actions attended daily, he had to report through the Secretariat and await instructions before memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, though the recorder of actions attended daily, he had to report through the Secretariat and await instructions before memorializing.

sentences.zh: 存乞復唐貞觀左右史執筆隨宰相入殿故事，神宗韙其言，聽直前奏事，自存始也。

translations.literal: Cun requested restoration of the Tang Zhenguan precedent whereby the left and right historians carried their brushes and followed the chief ministers into the hall; Shenzong approved his words and allowed direct presentation before the throne—beginning with Cun.
translations.idiomatic: Cun requested restoration of the Tang Zhenguan precedent whereby the left and right historians carried their brushes and followed the chief ministers into the hall; Shenzong approved his proposal and allowed direct presentation—beginning with Cun.

sentences.zh: 明年，以右正言、知制誥、同修國史兼判太常寺。

translations.literal: The next year he was made right remonstrance official, drafter of edicts, joint compiler of the national history, and concurrently administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made right remonstrance official, drafter of edicts, joint compiler of the national history, and concurrently administrator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 論圜丘合祭天地為非古，當親祠北郊如《周禮》。

translations.literal: He argued that the joint sacrifice of Heaven and Earth at the Circular Mound was not ancient practice and that the emperor should personally sacrifice at the Northern Suburb as in the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the joint sacrifice of Heaven and Earth at the Circular Mound was not ancient practice and that the emperor should personally sacrifice at the Northern Suburb as in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 官制行，神宗切於用人，存請自熙寧以來群臣緣論事得罪，或詿誤被斥而情實納忠非大過者，隨材召擢，以備官使。

translations.literal: When the new bureaucracy was implemented Shenzong was keen to employ men; Cun requested that from Xining onward officials who had offended through policy disputes or been dismissed through misunderstanding yet had in truth offered loyal counsel without grave fault be summoned and promoted according to ability to fill offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the new bureaucracy was implemented Shenzong was keen to employ men; Cun requested that from Xining onward officials who had offended through policy disputes or been dismissed through misunderstanding yet had in truth offered loyal counsel without grave fault be summoned and promoted according to ability to fill offices.

sentences.zh: 語合神宗意。

translations.literal: His words matched Shenzong's intent.
translations.idiomatic: His words matched Shenzong's intent.

sentences.zh: 收拔者甚眾。

translations.literal: Those recalled and promoted were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Very many were recalled and promoted.

sentences.zh: 又言：「赦令出上恩，而比歲議法治獄者，多乞不以赦降原減。

translations.literal: He also said: "Amnesties issue from imperial grace, yet in recent years those who deliberate on law in adjudicating cases often request that crimes not be remitted or reduced by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Amnesties issue from imperial grace, yet in recent years those who deliberate on law in adjudicating cases often request that crimes not be remitted or reduced by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 官司謁禁，本防請托，而吊死問疾，一切杜絕，皆非便也。」

translations.literal: Prohibitions on visiting officials were meant to guard against solicitation, yet to cut off entirely condolence calls and inquiries after the sick—none of this is expedient."
translations.idiomatic: Prohibitions on visiting officials were meant to guard against solicitation, yet to cut off entirely condolence calls and inquiries after the sick—none of this is expedient."

sentences.zh: 執政不悅。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were displeased.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷龍圖閣直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of the Kaifeng metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1082) he was transferred to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of the Kaifeng metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 京師並河居人，盜鑿汴堤以自廣，或請令培築復故，又按民廬侵官道者使撤之。

translations.literal: Residents along the capital's Bian Canal illicitly mined the dike to expand their properties; some proposed ordering restoration of the old embankment, while others investigated dwellings encroaching on the official roadway and demanded their demolition.
translations.idiomatic: Residents along the capital's Bian Canal illicitly mined the dike to expand their properties; some proposed ordering restoration of the old embankment, while others investigated dwellings encroaching on the official roadway and demanded their demolition.

sentences.zh: 二謀出自中人，既有詔矣。

translations.literal: Both schemes came from eunuchs, and an edict had already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Both schemes came from eunuchs, and an edict had already been issued.

sentences.zh: 存曰：「此吾職也。」

translations.literal: Cun said: "This is my responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: Cun said: "This is my responsibility."

sentences.zh: 入言之。

translations.literal: He entered the palace to speak on it.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the palace to speak on it.

sentences.zh: 即曰馳其役，都人歡呼相慶。

translations.literal: That very day the corvée was halted; the whole city shouted in celebration.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was immediately revoked and corvée halted; the whole city shouted in celebration.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士，改兵部尚書，轉戶部。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Privy Council, changed to Minister of War, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to academician of the Privy Council, changed to Minister of War, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 神宗崩，哲宗立，永裕陵財費，不逾時告備，宰相乘間復徙之兵部。

translations.literal: When Shenzong died and Zhezong succeeded, the expenses for Yongyu Tomb were reported ready in no time; the chief minister seized the occasion to move him back to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong died and Zhezong succeeded, the expenses for Yongyu Tomb were reported ready in no time; the chief minister seized the occasion to move him back to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 太僕寺請內外馬事得專達，毋隸駕部。

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Stud petitioned that matters concerning horses inside and outside the capital be reported directly, not subordinated to the Carriage Department.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of the Imperial Stud petitioned that matters concerning horses inside and outside the capital be reported directly, not subordinated to the Carriage Department.

sentences.zh: 存言：「如此，官制壞矣。

translations.literal: Cun said: "If this is done the bureaucratic system is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Cun said: "If this is done the bureaucratic system is ruined.

sentences.zh: 先帝正省、台、寺、監之職，使相臨制，不可徇有司自便，而隳已成之法。」

translations.literal: The late emperor straightened the duties of ministries, councils, courts, and directorates so they would oversee one another; we cannot indulge each office's convenience and ruin a system already established."
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor straightened the duties of ministries, councils, courts, and directorates so they would oversee one another; we cannot indulge each office's convenience and ruin a system already established."

sentences.zh: 元祐初，還戶部，固辭不受。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was returned to the Ministry of Revenue but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou (1086) he was returned to the Ministry of Revenue but firmly declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜中大夫、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Grandee of Persuasion and Right Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1087) he was appointed Grandee of Persuasion and Right Vice Councilor.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷左丞。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Left Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Left Vice Councilor.

sentences.zh: 有建議罷教畿內保甲者，存言：「今京師兵籍益削，又廢保甲不教，非國家根本久長之計。

translations.literal: When someone proposed abolishing training of metropolitan baojia militia, Cun said: "The capital's military registers are already thinning; to abolish baojia training as well is no plan for the state's long-term security.
translations.idiomatic: When someone proposed abolishing training of metropolitan baojia militia, Cun said: "The capital's military registers are already thinning; to abolish baojia training as well is no plan for the state's long-term security.

sentences.zh: 且先帝不憚艱難而為之，既已就緒，無故而廢之，不可。」

translations.literal: Moreover the late emperor did not shrink from difficulty to establish this; now that it is in order, to abandon it without cause is impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the late emperor did not shrink from difficulty to establish this; now that it is in order, to abandon it without cause is impossible."

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎韓維罷，存言：「去一正人，天下失望，忠黨沮氣，讒邪之人爭進矣。」

translations.literal: When Vice Director of the Chancellery Han Wei was dismissed, Cun said: "Remove one upright man and the empire loses hope, loyal partisans lose heart, and slanderers and villains will vie to advance."
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director of the Chancellery Han Wei was dismissed, Cun said: "Remove one upright man and the empire loses hope, loyal partisans lose heart, and slanderers and villains will vie to advance."

sentences.zh: 又論杜純不當罷侍御史，王覿不當罷諫官。

translations.literal: He also argued that Du Chun should not be removed as attendant censor and Wang Di should not be removed as remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Du Chun should not be removed as attendant censor and Wang Di should not be removed as remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 四方奏讞大辟，刑部援比請貸，都省屢以無可矜恕卻之。

translations.literal: When the regions reported capital cases, the Ministry of Justice cited precedents requesting leniency, but the Ministry repeatedly returned them on grounds that nothing warranted pity.
translations.idiomatic: When the regions reported capital cases, the Ministry of Justice cited precedents requesting leniency, but the Ministry repeatedly returned them on grounds that nothing warranted pity.

sentences.zh: 存曰：「此祖宗制也。

translations.literal: Cun said: "This is ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: Cun said: "This is ancestral institution.

sentences.zh: 有司欲生之，而朝廷破例殺之，可乎？」

translations.literal: The department wishes to spare them, yet the court breaks precedent to kill them—is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: The department wishes to spare them, yet the court breaks precedent to kill them—is that permissible?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「比廢進士專經一科，參以詩賦，失先帝黜詞律、崇經術之意。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Recently the specialist classics jinshi examination was abolished and poetry and rhapsody were mixed back in, contrary to the late emperor's purpose in dismissing lyric rules and elevating classical learning."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Recently the specialist classics jinshi examination was abolished and poetry and rhapsody were mixed back in, contrary to the late emperor's purpose in dismissing lyric rules and elevating classical learning."

sentences.zh: 河決而北幾十年，水官議還故道，存爭之曰：「故道已高，水性趨下，徒費財力，恐無成功。」

translations.literal: The Yellow River had been flowing north for nearly forty years; hydraulic officials proposed returning it to the old channel; Cun contended: "The old channel is already elevated while the water tends downward—only to waste resources with little hope of success."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River had been flowing north for nearly forty years; hydraulic officials proposed returning it to the old channel; Cun contended: "The old channel is already elevated while the water tends downward—only to waste resources with little hope of success."

sentences.zh: 卒輟其役。

translations.literal: The project was finally abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The project was finally abandoned.

sentences.zh: 蔡確以詩怨訕，存與范純仁欲薄其罪，確再貶新州，存亦罷，以端明殿學士知蔡州。

translations.literal: Cai Que, for verses of resentment and sneer, was to have his punishment eased by Cun and Fan Chunren; Que was banished again to Xinzhou and Cun was also dismissed, becoming academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que, for verses of resentment and mockery, was to have his punishment eased by Cun and Fan Chunren; Que was banished again to Xinzhou and Cun was also dismissed, becoming academician of the Duanming Hall and prefect of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始，存之徙兵部，確力也。

translations.literal: Initially when Cun was shifted to the Ministry of War, it was Que who pressed it.
translations.idiomatic: Initially when Cun was shifted to the Ministry of War, it was Que who had pressed for it.

sentences.zh: 至是，為確罷，士大夫善其能損怨。

translations.literal: Now dismissed because of Que, scholars praised his ability to set aside resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Now dismissed because of Que, scholars praised his ability to set aside resentment.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，加資政殿學士、知揚州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was given additional rank as academician of the Privy Council and made prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was given additional rank as academician of the Privy Council and made prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 揚、潤相去一水，用故相例，得歲時過家上冢，出賜錢給鄰里，又具酒食召會父老，親與酬酢，鄉黨傳為美談。

translations.literal: Yangzhou and Run Prefecture were separated by a single water; by precedent for former chief counselors he could visit home annually for tomb sweeping, distribute imperial bounty to neighbors, and host banquets for local elders, personally toasting them—talk of the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou and Run Prefecture were separated by a single stretch of water; by precedent for former chief counselors he could visit home annually for tomb sweeping, distribute imperial bounty to neighbors, and host banquets for local elders, personally toasting them—a story the countryside told with admiration.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時，在廷朋黨之論浸熾，存為哲宗言：「人臣朋黨，誠不可長，然或不察，則濫及善人。

translations.literal: At the time factional discourse in court was intensifying; Cun told Zhezong: "Factions among ministers truly must not grow, yet if one does not examine carefully the innocent may be swept up.
translations.idiomatic: At the time factional discourse in court was intensifying; Cun told Zhezong: "Factions among ministers truly must not grow, yet if one does not examine carefully the innocent may be swept up.

sentences.zh: 慶歷中，或指韓琦、富弼、范仲淹、歐陽修為黨，賴仁宗聖明，不為所惑。

translations.literal: In Qingli some pointed to Han Qi, Fu Bi, Fan Zhongyan, and Ouyang Xiu as a faction; fortunately Renzong was sagacious and was not misled.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli some pointed to Han Qi, Fu Bi, Fan Zhongyan, and Ouyang Xiu as a faction; fortunately Renzong was sagacious and was not misled.

sentences.zh: 今日果有進此說者，願陛下察之。」

translations.literal: If today anyone advances such talk, I pray Your Majesty discern it."
translations.idiomatic: If today anyone advances such talk, I pray Your Majesty discern it."

sentences.zh: 由是復與任事者戾，除知大名府，改知杭州。

translations.literal: Because of this he again clashed with those in office and was made prefect of Daming, then changed to prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he again clashed with those in office and was made prefect of Daming, then changed to prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，請老，提舉崇禧觀，遷右正議大夫致仕。

translations.literal: At the start of Shaosheng he requested retirement, was made overseer of the Chongxi Abbey, and promoted to Right Master of Persuasion with honorable retirement.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shaosheng (1094) he requested retirement, was made overseer of the Chongxi Abbey, and promoted to Right Master of Persuasion with honorable retirement.

sentences.zh: 舊制，當得東宮保傅，議者指存嘗議還西夏侵地，故殺其恩典，既而降通議大夫。

translations.literal: By old regulation he should have received grand protector posts in the Eastern Palace; critics cited his having urged returning Western Xia occupied land, so his grace was reduced, then lowered to Master of Exchange.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation he should have received grand protector posts in the Eastern Palace; critics cited his having urged returning Western Xia occupied land, so his grace was reduced, then lowered to Master of Exchange.

sentences.zh: 存嘗悼近世學士貴為公卿，而祭祀其先，但循庶人之制。

translations.literal: Cun had lamented that in recent times literati who rose to chief ministers still performed ancestral rites only by commoner custom.
translations.idiomatic: Cun had lamented that in recent times literati who rose to chief ministers still performed ancestral rites only by commoner custom.

sentences.zh: 及歸老築居，首營家廟。

translations.literal: When he retired and built his residence he first erected a family shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When he retired and built his residence he first erected a family shrine.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhongjingguo (1101) he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhongjingguo (1101) he died, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈左銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Silver Glory Grandee of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Silver Glory Grandee of Honor.

sentences.zh: 存性寬厚，平居恂恂，不為詭激之行，至其所守，確不可奪。

translations.literal: Cun's nature was generous and mild; in ordinary life he was deferential and made no showy or provocative acts, yet what he upheld could not be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Cun's nature was generous and mild; in ordinary life he was deferential and made no showy or provocative acts, yet what he upheld could not be shaken.

sentences.zh: 司馬光嘗曰：「並馳萬馬中能駐足者，其王存乎！」

translations.literal: Sima Guang once said: "Among ten thousand horses galloping abreast, the one who can rein in—is that not Wang Cun?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang once said: "Among ten thousand horses galloping abreast, the one who can rein in—is that not Wang Cun?"

sentences.zh: 孫固，字和父，鄭州管城人。

translations.literal: Sun Gu, style name Hefu, was a native of Guancheng in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gu, whose style name was Hefu, was a native of Guancheng in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼有立志。

translations.literal: From youth he formed high resolve.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he formed high resolve.

sentences.zh: 九歲讀《論語》，曰：「吾能行此。」

translations.literal: At nine he read the Analects and said: "I can practice this."
translations.idiomatic: At nine he read the Analects and said: "I can practice this."

sentences.zh: 徂徠石介一見，以公輔期之。

translations.literal: Cuzai Shi Jie upon one meeting looked to him as a future chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Cuzai Shi Jie, upon a single meeting, looked to him as a future chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，調磁州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Cizhou's household office.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Cizhou's household office.

sentences.zh: 從平貝州，為文彥博言脅從罔治之義，與彥博意協，故但誅首惡，余無所及。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Bei Prefecture he explained to Wen Yanbo the principle of not prosecuting the coerced; Yanbo agreed, so only the ringleaders were punished and the rest untouched.
translations.idiomatic: Following the pacification of Bei Prefecture he explained to Wen Yanbo the principle of not prosecuting the coerced; Yanbo agreed, so only the ringleaders were punished and the rest went untouched.

sentences.zh: 轉霍邑令，遷秘書丞，為審刑詳議官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Huoyi, promoted to Secretariat director, and made detailed reviewer in the Court for Scrutiny of Offenses.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Huoyi, promoted to Secretariat director, and made detailed reviewer in the Court for Scrutiny of Offenses.

sentences.zh: 宰相韓琦知其賢，諭使來見，固不肯往。

translations.literal: Chief Counselor Han Qi knew his talent and urged him to call; Gu firmly refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Counselor Han Qi knew his talent and urged him to call; Gu firmly refused to go.

sentences.zh: 琦益器重之，引為編修中書諸房文字。

translations.literal: Qi valued him all the more and brought him in as compiler of documents for the various bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Qi valued him all the more and brought him in as compiler of documents for the various bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 治平中，神宗為潁王，以固侍講；

translations.literal: During Zhiping, when Shenzong was Prince of Ying, Gu served as his lecturer;
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiping, when Shenzong was Prince of Ying, Gu served as his lecturer;

sentences.zh: 及為皇太子，又為侍讀。

translations.literal: when he became crown prince, Gu again served as reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: when he became crown prince, Gu again served as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 至即位，擢工部郎中、天章閣待制、知通進銀台司。

translations.literal: Upon accession he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works, awaiting draft in the Heavenly Records Pavilion, and overseer of the Silver Terrace Gateway Office.
translations.idiomatic: Upon accession he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works, awaiting draft in the Heavenly Records Pavilion, and overseer of the Silver Terrace Gateway Office.

sentences.zh: 種諤取綏州，固知神宗志欲經略西夏，欲先事以戒，即上言：「待遠人宜示之信，今無名舉兵，非計之得。

translations.literal: When Zhong E took Suizhou, Gu knew Shenzong wished to manage Western Xia affairs and wished to warn him in advance, so he memorialized: "In dealing with distant peoples one should show trust; to raise troops without cause is no worthy plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong E took Suizhou, Gu knew Shenzong wished to manage Western Xia affairs and wished to warn him in advance, so he memorialized: "In dealing with distant peoples one should show trust; to raise troops without cause is no worthy plan.

sentences.zh: 願以漢韓安國、魏相、唐魏征論兵之略，參校同異，則是非炳然矣。

translations.literal: I beg that the military discussions of Han Anguo of Han, Wei Xiang of Wei, and Wei Zheng of Tang be collated for comparison, and right and wrong will stand clear.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the military discussions of Han Anguo of Han, Wei Xiang of Wei, and Wei Zheng of Tang be collated for comparison, and right and wrong will stand clear.

sentences.zh: 兵，兇器也，動不可妄，妄動將有悔。」

translations.literal: Arms are an inauspicious instrument; to move them must not be rash—rash movement brings regret."
translations.idiomatic: Arms are an inauspicious instrument; to move them must not be rash—rash movement brings regret."

sentences.zh: 大臣惡其說，出知澶州。

translations.literal: Great ministers detested his view and he was sent out as prefect of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers detested his view and he was sent out as prefect of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還知審刑院，復領銀台、封駁兼侍讀，判少府監。

translations.literal: Called back to head the Court for Scrutiny, again overseeing Silver Terrace and seal review, lecturer-in-waiting, and administrator of the Court of Imperial Works.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to head the Court for Scrutiny, again overseeing Silver Terrace and seal review, lecturer-in-waiting, and administrator of the Court of Imperial Works.

sentences.zh: 神宗問：「王安石可相否？」

translations.literal: Shenzong asked: "Can Wang Anshi serve as chief counselor?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong asked: "Can Wang Anshi serve as chief counselor?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安石文行甚高，處侍從獻納之職，可矣。

translations.literal: He answered: "Anshi's learning and conduct are very lofty; in attendance and remonstrance he suffices.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Anshi's learning and conduct are very lofty; in attendance and remonstrance he suffices.

sentences.zh: 宰相自有其度，安石狷狹少容。

translations.literal: Chief counselor has its own measure; Anshi is narrow-minded with little tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: Chief counselor has its own measure; Anshi is narrow-minded with little tolerance.

sentences.zh: 必欲求賢相，呂公著、司馬光、韓維其人也。」

translations.literal: If you truly wish a worthy counselor, Lü Gongzhu, Sima Guang, and Han Wei are the men."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly wish a worthy counselor, Lü Gongzhu, Sima Guang, and Han Wei are the men."

sentences.zh: 凡四問，皆以此對。

translations.literal: Four times he was asked and each time answered thus.
translations.idiomatic: Four times he was asked and each time answered thus.

sentences.zh: 及安石當國，更法度，固數議事不合；

translations.literal: When Anshi held power and reformed institutions, Gu repeatedly disputed and disagreed;
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi held power and reformed institutions, Gu repeatedly disputed and disagreed;

sentences.zh: 青苗法出，又極陳其不便。

translations.literal: when the Green Sprouts law was issued he vigorously stated its inconveniences.
translations.idiomatic: when the Green Sprouts law was issued he vigorously stated its inconveniences.

sentences.zh: 及韓琦疏至，神宗感動，謂固曰：「朕熟計之，誠不便。」

translations.literal: When Han Qi's memorial arrived Shenzong was moved and told Gu: "I have weighed it carefully—it is truly inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi's memorial arrived Shenzong was moved and told Gu: "I have weighed it carefully—it is truly inconvenient."

sentences.zh: 固出語執政曰：「及上有意，宜亟圖之，以福天下。」

translations.literal: Gu went out and told the chief ministers: "While His Majesty is minded to it, you should quickly plan it for the empire's blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Gu went out and told the chief ministers: "While His Majesty is minded to it, you should quickly plan it for the empire's blessing."

sentences.zh: 既而竟從安石。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they followed Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end they followed Anshi.

sentences.zh: 固復領銀臺司。

translations.literal: Gu again oversaw the Silver Terrace Office.
translations.idiomatic: Gu again oversaw the Silver Terrace Office.

sentences.zh: 孔文仲對制策忤時政，報罷。

translations.literal: Kong Wenzhong's policy response examination offended current politics and he was failed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenzhong's policy response examination offended current politics and he was failed.

sentences.zh: 固言：「陛下以名求士，而士以實應，今反過之，何哉？

translations.literal: Gu said: "Your Majesty seeks scholars by reputation and scholars respond with substance; now this is reversed—how so?
translations.idiomatic: Gu said: "Your Majesty seeks scholars by reputation and scholars respond with substance; now this is reversed—how so?

sentences.zh: 今謂文仲之言以惑天下，臣恐天下不惑文仲之言，以文仲之黜為惑也。」

translations.literal: To say Wenzhong's words mislead the empire—I fear the empire will not be misled by Wenzhong's words but will be misled by Wenzhong's dismissal."
translations.idiomatic: To say Wenzhong's words mislead the empire—I fear the empire will not be misled by Wenzhong's words but will be misled by Wenzhong's dismissal."

sentences.zh: 胡宗愈坐言事逐，蘇頌、陳薦以論李定罷，固皆引誼爭之。

translations.literal: Hu Zongyu was dismissed for remonstrance; Su Song and Chen Jian were removed for criticizing Li Ding—Gu all cited righteousness to dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zongyu was dismissed for remonstrance; Su Song and Chen Jian were removed for criticizing Li Ding—Gu all cited righteousness to dispute.

sentences.zh: 時議尊僖祖為始祖，固議曰：「漢高以得天下與商、周異，故太上皇不得為始封；

translations.literal: At the time deliberation honored Emperor Xianzu as founding ancestor; Gu argued: "Gaozu of Han differed from Shang and Zhou in gaining the empire, so the Great Supreme could not be founding fief;
translations.idiomatic: At the time deliberation honored Emperor Xianzu as founding ancestor; Gu argued: "Gaozu of Han differed from Shang and Zhou in gaining the empire, so the Great Supreme could not be founding fief;

sentences.zh: 光武中興，不敢祖舂陵而祖高帝。

translations.literal: Guangwu at restoration dared not take Chunling as ancestor but took Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu at restoration dared not take Chunling as ancestor but took Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 宋有天下，傳之萬世，太祖功也，不當替其祀；

translations.literal: Song received the empire to pass to ten thousand generations—Taizu's achievement; his sacrifices must not be displaced;
translations.idiomatic: Song received the empire to pass to ten thousand generations—Taizu's achievement; his sacrifices must not be displaced;

sentences.zh: 請以為始祖，而為僖祖別立廟。

translations.literal: I ask that he be taken as founding ancestor, and that a separate temple be erected for Xizu.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that Taizu be recognized as founding ancestor and that a separate temple be built for Xizu.

sentences.zh: 禘祫之日，奉其祧主東向以伸其尊，合所謂祖以孫尊、孫以祖屈之意。」

translations.literal: On the days of di and xia, his ancestral tablet would be placed facing east to extend his honor, matching the meaning of the saying that the ancestor is honored through the grandson and the grandson yields to the ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: On the great seasonal sacrifices, Xizu's tablet would face east to show his dignity, in keeping with the principle that the ancestor is exalted through the grandson while the grandson defers to the ancestor.

sentences.zh: 韓琦見而嘆曰：「孫公此議，足以不朽矣。」

translations.literal: When Han Qi saw it he sighed and said, "Master Sun's proposal is enough to secure immortality."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi read it, he sighed and said, "Master Sun's proposal alone would be enough to make his name immortal."

sentences.zh: 加龍圖閣直學士、知真定府。

translations.literal: He was made Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-in-Attendance and prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Dragon Diagram Hall Academician-in-Attendance and made prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 遼人盜耕解子平地，歲且久，吏爭弗能還。

translations.literal: Liao people had encroached to farm Jiezi Pingdi for years, and officials disputed it but could not recover it.
translations.idiomatic: For years the Liao had been farming encroached land at Jiezi Pingdi, and local officials could not win it back despite repeated disputes.

sentences.zh: 固微得其要領，折愧之，正疆地二百里。

translations.literal: Gu subtly grasped the essentials, shamed them into yielding, and rectified the border by two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Gu quietly mastered the essentials of the case, shamed the Liao into backing down, and restored two hundred li of borderland.

sentences.zh: 熙寧末，以樞密直學士知開封府。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xining era he served as Secretariat Direct Academician and prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xining era he was made Secretariat Direct Academician and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanfeng era he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時征安南，建順州，其地瘴癘不堪守，固請棄之，內徙者二萬戶。

translations.literal: At the time the campaign against Annan had established Shun Prefecture; the place was malarial and unbearable to hold, and Gu urged abandoning it, moving inward twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Annan, Shun Prefecture had been established, but the region was too malarial to garrison. Gu urged that it be abandoned and twenty thousand households be resettled inland.

sentences.zh: 諜者告夏人幽其主，神宗欲西討，固數言舉兵易，解禍難。

translations.literal: Spies reported that the Xia had imprisoned their ruler; Emperor Shenzong wished to campaign west, and Gu repeatedly said that raising troops is easy but resolving the disaster is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported that the Xia had imprisoned their ruler. When Emperor Shenzong wanted to launch a western campaign, Gu repeatedly warned that it is easy to start a war but hard to end the trouble it brings.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「夏有釁不取，則為遼人所有，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said, "When Xia offers a pretext and we do not seize it, it will fall to the Liao—we cannot let it slip."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said, "When Xia gives us a pretext and we fail to act, the Liao will take it instead. We cannot miss this chance.

sentences.zh: 固曰：「必不得已，請聲其罪薄伐之，分裂其地，使其酋長自守焉。」

translations.literal: Gu said, "If it truly cannot be avoided, please proclaim their crimes and make a limited campaign, partition their territory, and let their chieftains hold it themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied, "If we truly have no choice, at least proclaim their crimes and wage a limited campaign. Partition their territory and let their chieftains hold each part on their own.

sentences.zh: 神宗笑曰：「此真酈生之說爾。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong laughed and said, "This is truly the talk of Master Li."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong laughed and said, "That is exactly the sort of thing Li Sheng would have said.

sentences.zh: 時執政有言便當直度河，不可留行。

translations.literal: At the time those in power said they should cross the river at once and must not delay.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power at the time argued that the army should cross the river immediately and must not linger.

sentences.zh: 固曰：「然則孰為陛下任此者？」

translations.literal: Gu said, "Then who will Your Majesty entrust with this?"
translations.idiomatic: Gu asked, "Then whom will Your Majesty put in charge of it?

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「朕已屬李憲。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said, "I have already assigned Li Xian."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "I have already entrusted it to Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 固曰：「伐國，大事也，豈可使宦官為之！

translations.literal: Gu said, "Attacking a state is a great matter—how can a eunuch be made to do it!
translations.idiomatic: Gu protested, "Invading a state is a grave undertaking. How can it be entrusted to a eunuch!

sentences.zh: 今陛下任李憲，則士大夫孰肯為用乎？」

translations.literal: Now if Your Majesty assigns Li Xian, which scholar-official will be willing to serve?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty puts Li Xian in command, which scholar-official will be willing to serve under him?

sentences.zh: 神宗不悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 他日，固又曰：「今五路進師而無大帥，就使成功，兵必為亂。」

translations.literal: Another day Gu again said, "Now five routes advance armies without a supreme commander; even if they succeed, the troops will surely turn to disorder."
translations.idiomatic: On another day Gu warned again, "Five columns are advancing without a supreme commander. Even if they win, the armies will surely fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「大帥誠難其人。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said, "A supreme commander is truly hard to find."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It really is hard to find the right supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 呂公著曰：「既無其人，曷若已之。」

translations.literal: Lü Gongzhu said, "Since there is no such person, why not stop it?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongzhu said, "If there is no suitable man, why not call the campaign off?

sentences.zh: 固曰：「公著言是也。」

translations.literal: Gu said, "Gongzhu's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "Gongzhu is right.

sentences.zh: 初議五路入討，會於靈州，李憲由熙河入，輒不赴靈州，乃自開蘭、會，欲以弭責。

translations.literal: At first the plan was for five routes to enter in punitive attack and meet at Lingzhou; Li Xian entered by the Xihe route but abruptly did not go to Lingzhou, and on his own opened Lan and Hui, intending thereby to escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: The original plan called for five columns to converge on Lingzhou. Li Xian entered through the Xihe route but never went to Lingzhou. Instead he seized Lan and Hui on his own, hoping that would shield him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 固曰：「兵法期而後至者斬。

translations.literal: Gu said, "In military law, one who is late after the appointed time is beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "Military law says that anyone who arrives after the appointed time is to be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 今諸路皆進，而憲獨不行，雖得蘭、會，罪不可赦。」

translations.literal: Now every route has advanced while Xian alone did not go; though he gained Lan and Hui, the crime cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Every column has advanced while Xian alone has not. Even if he captured Lan and Hui, his offense cannot be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 神宗不聽，其後師果無功。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong would not listen; afterward the armies indeed achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen, and in the end the campaign failed completely.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「朕始以孫固言為迂，今悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said, "At first I thought Sun Gu's words pedantic; now regret comes too late."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said, "At first I thought Sun Gu was being pedantic. Now it is too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 改太中大夫、樞密副使，進知院事，以疾避位，拜觀文殿學士、知河陽，尋提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: He was changed to Grandee of Palace Attendance and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to Director of the Bureau, then because of illness avoided office and was made Wenyuan Hall Academician and prefect of Heyang, soon after superintendent of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grandee of Palace Attendance and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then advanced to Director of the bureau. Illness forced him to step aside, and he was made Wenyuan Hall Academician and prefect of Heyang, then soon superintendent of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，以正議大夫知河南府，徙鄭州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne he was made Grandee of Righteous Counsel and prefect of Henan, then transferred to Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Gu was made Grandee of Righteous Counsel and prefect of Henan, then transferred to Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，召除侍讀、提舉中太一宮，遂拜門下侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou he was summoned and made Imperial Reader and superintendent of the Central Grand Unity Palace, then appointed Vice Minister of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanyou he was recalled, made Imperial Reader and superintendent of the Central Grand Unity Palace, and then appointed Vice Minister of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 哲宗與太皇太后矜其年高，每朝會豫節拜儀，聽休於幄次。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong and the Grand Empress Dowager took pity on his advanced age; at each court assembly they allowed him to abbreviate the bowing rites and rest in the side pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong and the Grand Empress Dowager, mindful of his age, let him shorten the bowing rites at court and rest in the side pavilion.

sentences.zh: 固數乞骸骨，太皇太后曰：「卿，先帝在東宮時舊臣。

translations.literal: Gu repeatedly begged to retire; the Grand Empress Dowager said, "You are an old minister from when the late emperor was in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gu repeatedly asked to retire. The Grand Empress Dowager said, "You are an old minister from when the late emperor was still heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 今帝新聽政，勉留輔導；

translations.literal: The present emperor has newly taken charge of government—urge yourself to remain and guide him;
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor has only just begun to rule. I urge you to stay and guide him.

sentences.zh: 或體中未安，取文書於家治之可也。」

translations.literal: or if your body is not at ease, you may take documents home to handle them."
translations.idiomatic: If you are unwell, you may take documents home and handle them there.

sentences.zh: 固感激，強起視事，復知樞密院事，累官右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Gu was moved, forced himself to rise and attend to affairs, again became Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and cumulatively reached Right Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, Gu forced himself back to duty, again became Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and eventually rose to Right Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanyou he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 哲宗、太皇太后皆出聲泣。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong and the Grand Empress Dowager both wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Both Emperor Zhezong and the Grand Empress Dowager wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 時文彥博致仕歸洛，將宴餞崇政殿，以固在殯，罷之。

translations.literal: At the time Wen Yanbo had retired and returned to Luoyang; a farewell banquet was to be held in Chongzheng Hall, but because Gu lay in mourning it was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo had recently retired to Luoyang, and a farewell banquet was planned in Chongzheng Hall, but it was canceled because Gu's body still lay in state.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝二日，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰溫靖。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for two days; he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies, and his posthumous title was Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were suspended for two days. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and given the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 固宅心誠粹，不喜矯亢，與人居久而益信，故更歷夷險，而不為人所疾害。

translations.literal: Gu's inner mind was sincere and pure; he did not like affectation or arrogance, and the longer he dwelt with others the more they trusted him, so through ease and peril alike he was not resented or harmed by others.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was sincere and pure at heart, disliked pretension and arrogance, and grew more trusted the longer people knew him. Through good times and bad he was never resented or harmed.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「人當以聖賢為師，一節之士，不足學也。」

translations.literal: He once said, "One ought to take sages and worthies as teachers; a man of but one virtue is not worth studying."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "People should take sages and worthies as their teachers. A man who excels in only one virtue is not worth imitating.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「以愛親之心愛其君，則無不盡矣。」

translations.literal: He also said, "If one loves one's ruler with the heart with which one loves one's parents, there is nothing one will not exhaust for him."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Serve your ruler with the same devotion you give your parents, and you will hold nothing back.

sentences.zh: 司馬光退處，固每勸神宗召歸；

translations.literal: When Sima Guang had withdrawn, Gu repeatedly urged Emperor Shenzong to recall him;
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang had retired from office, Gu repeatedly urged Emperor Shenzong to recall him.

sentences.zh: 及光為陳州，過鄭，固與論天下大事至數十，曰：「公行且相，宜視先後緩急審處之。」

translations.literal: when Guang became prefect of Chen and passed through Zheng, Gu discussed great affairs of the realm with him dozens of times and said, "Sir, you are about to become chief minister—you should weigh what comes first and last, what is urgent and what is slow, and handle them carefully."
translations.idiomatic: When Guang became prefect of Chen and passed through Zheng on his way, Gu discussed the great affairs of the realm with him dozens of times and said, "You are about to become chief minister. Weigh priorities carefully and handle each matter in its proper order.

sentences.zh: 傅堯俞銘其墓曰：「司馬公之清節，孫公之淳德，蓋所謂不言而信者也。」

translations.literal: Fu Yaoyu inscribed his tomb: "Master Sima's pure integrity and Master Sun's simple virtue are what is called being trusted without speaking."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yaoyu wrote on his tomb, "Master Sima's pure integrity and Master Sun's simple virtue are what people mean when they speak of trust earned without words.

sentences.zh: 世以為確論。

translations.literal: The age regarded it as a sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations regarded that as a sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 紹聖時奪遺澤，元符二年，奪所贈官，列元祐黨籍。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era his posthumous favors were stripped; in the second year of Yuanfu his conferred offices were taken away and he was entered on the Yuanyou faction register.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng his posthumous honors were revoked. In the second year of Yuanfu his conferred offices were stripped and he was entered on the Yuanyou faction register.

sentences.zh: 政和中，徽宗以固嘗為神宗宮僚，特出籍，悉還所奪。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era, because Gu had once been a palace attendant of Emperor Shenzong, Huizong specially removed him from the register and fully restored what had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe era, because Gu had once served in Shenzong's palace staff, Huizong specially removed him from the register and restored everything that had been taken away.

sentences.zh: 趙瞻，字大觀，其先亳州永城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhan, style name Daguan, his ancestors were people of Yongcheng in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhan, whose style name was Daguan, came from a family originally of Yongcheng in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 父剛，太子賓客，徙鳳翔之盩厔。

translations.literal: His father Gang was a Guest of the Heir Apparent and moved to Zhouzhi in Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gang had been Guest of the Heir Apparent and later moved the family to Zhouzhi in Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 瞻舉進士第，調孟州司戶參軍，移萬泉令。

translations.literal: Zhan passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as Revenue Section aide in Meng Prefecture, and transferred to magistrate of Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Revenue Section aide in Meng Prefecture, and later became magistrate of Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 捐圭田修學宮，士自遠而至。

translations.literal: He donated his gui fields to repair the school, and scholars came from afar.
translations.idiomatic: He donated his gui fields to rebuild the county school, and scholars came from far away to study there.

sentences.zh: 改知夏縣，作八監堂，書古賢令長治跡以自監。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Xia County, built the Hall of Eight Mirrors, and wrote the governing traces of ancient worthy magistrates to monitor himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Xia County, built the Hall of Eight Mirrors, and inscribed the records of ancient worthy magistrates there to hold himself accountable.

sentences.zh: 又以秘書丞知永昌縣，築六堰灌田，歲省科斂數十萬，水訟咸息，民以比召、杜。

translations.literal: He also served as Secretariat Assistant and prefect of Yongchang County, built six weirs to irrigate fields, saved hundreds of thousands in annual tax levies, water lawsuits all ceased, and the people compared him to Zhao and Du.
translations.idiomatic: As Secretariat Assistant he also governed Yongchang County, where he built six irrigation weirs. Annual tax levies fell by hundreds of thousands, water disputes died away, and the people compared him to the famous administrators Zhao and Du.

sentences.zh: 升太常博士，知威州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瞻以威、茂雜群獠，險而難守，不若合之而建郡於汶川，條著其詳，為《西山別錄》。

translations.literal: Zhan held that Wei and Mao were mixed with many Liao tribes, perilous and hard to hold; it would be better to combine them and establish a prefecture at Wenchuan, setting out the details in clauses and composing Separate Records of the Western Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao argued that Wei and Mao were entangled with many tribal peoples, too rugged to defend separately. He proposed merging them into a new prefecture at Wenchuan and laid out the plan in detail in his Separate Records of the Western Mountains.

sentences.zh: 後熙寧中，朝廷經理西南，就瞻取其書考焉。

translations.literal: Later in the Xining era, when the court administered the southwest, it took Zhao's book for reference.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Xining reforms, when the court reorganized the southwest, it consulted Zhao's book.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue's Fields Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue's Fields Section.

sentences.zh: 英宗治平初，自都官員外郎除侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Yingzong's Zhiping era he was made Attending Censor from Assistant in the Capital Section.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Yingzong's Zhiping era he was promoted from Assistant in the Capital Section to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「英斷獨化，人主至權也。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying, "Resolute judgment acting alone is the sovereign's supreme power.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Resolute judgment exercised on one's own is the ruler's supreme authority.

sentences.zh: 審至權者，當主以天下之大公，揆以天下之正論，如是而後權可一也。

translations.literal: One who examines this supreme power should take as master the great public good of the realm and measure by the correct discourse of the realm; only then can power be unified.
translations.idiomatic: To wield that authority rightly, one must be guided by the great public good of the realm and measured by its shared standards of right judgment. Only then can power be truly unified.

sentences.zh: 若夫積久之敝，陛下其思焉。

translations.literal: As for long-accumulated abuses, Your Majesty should reflect on them.
translations.idiomatic: As for abuses that have accumulated over many years, Your Majesty should give them careful thought.

sentences.zh: 刑賞施設之失，可革則革；

translations.literal: Errors in punishments, rewards, and institutions—what can be reformed, reform;
translations.idiomatic: Where punishments, rewards, and institutions have gone wrong, reform what can be reformed.

sentences.zh: 號令言動之過，可止則止。

translations.literal: faults in edicts, words, and conduct—what can be stopped, stop.
translations.idiomatic: Where edicts, words, and conduct have gone astray, stop what can be stopped.

sentences.zh: 輔相賴其用，宜責其效；

translations.literal: Chancellors are relied on for their use—they should be charged with results;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors are employed for their service; hold them accountable for results.

sentences.zh: 臺諫知其才，宜信其說。

translations.literal: censors know their talent—they should be trusted in their statements.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate knows their talent; trust what they say.

sentences.zh: 兵柄宜削諸宦官，邊議宜付諸宿將。

translations.literal: Military authority should be stripped from eunuchs; frontier deliberations should be entrusted to veteran generals.
translations.idiomatic: Strip eunuchs of military authority and entrust frontier policy to veteran generals.

sentences.zh: 蓋權不可矯而為也，以從天下之望耳。」

translations.literal: For power cannot be forced contrary to reason; it is only to follow what the realm hopes for."
translations.idiomatic: Authority cannot be bent by force. It must follow what the realm expects of its ruler.

sentences.zh: 英宗稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong praised the memorial.

sentences.zh: 久之，詔遣內侍王昭明等四人為陝西諸路鈐轄，招撫諸部。

translations.literal: After some time an edict sent the inner attendants Wang Zhaoming and three others as supervisory commissioners of the Shaanxi routes to pacify and win over the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict dispatched the inner attendants Wang Zhaoming and three others as supervisory commissioners on the Shaanxi frontier to pacify the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 瞻以唐用宦者為觀軍容、宣慰等使，後世以為至戒，宜追還內侍，責成守臣，章三上，言甚激切。

translations.literal: Zhan cited how the Tang used eunuchs as Army Supervisory Commissioners and Pacification Commissioners, which later ages took as the gravest warning; the inner attendants should be recalled and frontier defense charged to the guarding officials. He submitted three memorials, his words very forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cited how the Tang had used eunuchs as army supervisory and pacification commissioners, a practice later ages regarded as the gravest warning. He urged that the inner attendants be recalled and frontier defense left to the local commanders. He submitted three forceful memorials on the matter.

sentences.zh: 會文彥博、孫沔經略西夏，別遣馮京安撫諸路，瞻又請罷京使，專委宿將。

translations.literal: When Wen Yanbo and Sun Mian were commissioned to administer the Western Xia, Feng Jing was separately sent to pacify the various routes; Zhan again asked that Jing's mission be ended and veteran generals alone be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo and Sun Mian were put in charge of the Western Xia frontier, Feng Jing was separately sent to pacify the routes. Zhao again asked that Feng Jing's mission be canceled and the work entrusted to veteran generals alone.

sentences.zh: 夏人入侵王官，慶帥孫長卿不能御，加長卿集賢院學士，瞻言長卿當黜不宜賞，賞罰倒置。

translations.literal: The Xia invaded Wangguan; the Qingzhou commander Sun Changqing could not repel them, yet Changqing was given the title Academician of the Hall for Advancing Worthies. Zhan said Changqing ought to be dismissed, not rewarded—rewards and punishments were inverted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided Wangguan, the Qingzhou commander Sun Changqing failed to repel them, yet he was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Advancing Worthies. Zhao protested that he should have been dismissed, not rewarded, calling it a reversal of reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 京東盜賊數起，瞻請易置曹、濮守臣之不才者，未報。

translations.literal: Bandits in the eastern capital region rose repeatedly; Zhan asked to replace the incompetent guarding officials of Cao and Pu, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry flared repeatedly in the eastern capital region. Zhao asked that incompetent prefects in Cao and Pu be replaced, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 乃求退，力言追還昭明等，英宗改容，納其言。

translations.literal: He then sought to retire and spoke forcefully on recalling Zhaoming and the others; Emperor Yingzong changed expression and accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to retire and spoke forcefully again about recalling Zhaoming and the others. Emperor Yingzong's expression changed, and he accepted Zhao's advice.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，京師大水，詔百官言事，多留中，瞻請「悉出章疏，付兩省詳擇以聞」，從之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year the capital suffered great floods; the emperor ordered all officials to speak on affairs, but many memorials were held within the palace. Zhan asked that "all memorials be released and handed to the two departments for detailed selection and report," and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the capital was struck by severe flooding. The emperor ordered all officials to submit memorials, but many were held back in the palace. Zhao asked that every memorial be released to the two departments for review and report, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 時議追崇濮安懿王，瞻引漢師丹、董宏事，謂其屬薛溫其曰：「事將類此，吾必以死爭，固吾所也。」

translations.literal: At the time there was debate over posthumously honoring Prince Anyi of Pu; Zhan cited the Han cases of Shi Dan and Dong Hong and told his subordinate Xue Wenqi, "The affair will resemble this—I must dispute it to the death; that is my fixed resolve."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was debating posthumous honors for Prince Anyi of Pu. Zhao cited the Han precedents of Shi Dan and Dong Hong and told his subordinate Xue Wenqi, "This affair will be like those cases. I will dispute it to the death. That is my firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 中書請安懿王稱親，瞻爭曰：「仁宗既下明詔子陛下，議者顧惑禮律所生所養之名，妄相訾難，彼明知禮無兩父貳斬之義，敢裂一字之詞，以亂厥真。

translations.literal: The Secretariat asked that Prince Anyi be called "kin"; Zhan disputed, saying, "Emperor Renzong already issued a clear edict making Your Majesty his son. The debaters only fix on the ritual terms for biological and adopted parentage and recklessly criticize one another. They clearly know ritual has no meaning of two fathers or two mourning garments, yet dare to split a single word to confuse the truth.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat asked that Prince Anyi be addressed as the emperor's kin, Zhao objected, "Emperor Renzong already issued a clear edict naming Your Majesty his son. The debaters fix only on ritual terms for biological and adoptive parentage and recklessly attack one another. They know perfectly well that ritual allows no two fathers or two mourning garments, yet they dare twist a single word to overturn the truth.

sentences.zh: 且文有去婦出母者，去已非婦，出不為母，辭窮直書，豈足援以斷大議哉？

translations.literal: Moreover the text has one who dismissed his wife and expelled his mother—once dismissed she is no longer wife, once expelled she is no longer mother; the language at an impasse is written plainly. How can that suffice to decide a great debate?
translations.idiomatic: The ritual text even says that a man who dismisses his wife and expels his mother has neither a wife nor a mother in name. That passage was written in plain desperation. How can it decide a question of state?

sentences.zh: 臣請與之庭辨，以定邪正。」

translations.literal: Your subject asks to dispute with them in court to settle what is crooked and what is straight."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to debate them openly in court and settle what is right and what is wrong.

sentences.zh: 已而皇太后手書尊王為皇，瞻嘆曰：「向者太后切責大臣，議乃得罷。

translations.literal: Before long the Grand Empress Dowager wrote by hand to honor the prince as emperor; Zhan sighed and said, "Formerly the Empress Dowager sternly reproached the great ministers and the debate was able to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Grand Empress Dowager wrote by hand to honor the prince as emperor. Zhao sighed and said, "Earlier the empress dowager had sternly rebuked the chief ministers, and the debate was halted.

sentences.zh: 今邪臣與中官交締，歸過至尊而自為之地，吾與首議之臣，不並生矣！」

translations.literal: Now wicked ministers and inner attendants are intertwined; they shift blame onto the supreme sovereign and make room for themselves—I and the ministers who led the debate cannot live together!"
translations.idiomatic: Now wicked ministers and palace eunuchs are in league. They shift the blame onto Your Majesty while carving out their own advantage. The ministers who led the opposition and I cannot both survive!

sentences.zh: 因復力陳。

translations.literal: He therefore again stated his case forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his argument again with all his force.

sentences.zh: 會假太常少卿接契丹賀正使，入對，英宗問前事，對曰：「陛下為仁宗子，而濮王又稱皇考，則是二父，二父非禮。」

translations.literal: He happened to be acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to receive the Khitan New Year's congratulatory envoy; entering audience, Emperor Yingzong asked about the earlier affair, and he replied, "Your Majesty is Emperor Renzong's son, yet Prince Pu is also called Imperial Father—then there are two fathers, and two fathers are not ritual."
translations.idiomatic: He was temporarily serving as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to receive the Khitan New Year's envoy. At audience Emperor Yingzong asked about the earlier affair, and Zhao replied, "Your Majesty is Emperor Renzong's son, yet Prince Pu is also to be called Imperial Father. That would mean two fathers, and two fathers violate ritual.

sentences.zh: 英宗曰：「御史嘗見朕欲皇考濮王乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong said, "Censor, have you ever seen Us wish to make Prince Pu Imperial Father?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Censor, have you ever seen me wish to make Prince Pu my imperial father?

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「此乃大臣之議，陛下未嘗自言。」

translations.literal: Zhan said, "This is the great ministers' proposal; Your Majesty has never spoken of it yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "This is the ministers' proposal. Your Majesty has never said so yourself.

sentences.zh: 英宗曰：「是中書過耳，朕自數歲時，先帝養為子，豈敢稱濮考？」

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong said, "That is only the Secretariat's fault. From the time I was several years old the late emperor raised me as his son—how would I dare call Prince Pu father?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is only the Secretariat's doing. From childhood the late emperor raised me as his son. How could I dare call Prince Pu my father?

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「臣請退諭中書，作詔以曉天下。」

translations.literal: Zhan said, "Your subject asks to withdraw and instruct the Secretariat to draft an edict to enlighten all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Then let me withdraw and instruct the Secretariat to draft an edict clarifying this for the realm.

sentences.zh: 時連日晦冥，英宗指天示瞻曰：「天道如此，安敢妄為褒尊。

translations.literal: At the time for days the sky was dark; Emperor Yingzong pointed to Heaven and showed Zhan, saying, "Heaven's way is like this—how would I dare rashly grant exalted honors?
translations.idiomatic: For days the sky had been dark and ominous. The emperor pointed to Heaven and said to Zhao, "Heaven's warning is plain. How could I dare rashly grant exalted honors?

sentences.zh: 朕意已決，無庸宣告。」

translations.literal: My mind is already decided; there is no need to proclaim it."
translations.idiomatic: My mind is already made up. There is no need for a proclamation.

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「陛下祗畏天戒，不以私妨公，甚盛德也。」

translations.literal: Zhan said, "Your Majesty reverently fears Heaven's warning and does not let private feeling obstruct the public good—this is very great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Your Majesty reverently heeds Heaven's warning and will not let private feeling obstruct the public good. That is magnificent virtue.

sentences.zh: 及使還，聞呂誨等諫濮議皆罷去，乞與同貶，不報。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission he heard that Lü Hui and others who remonstrated on the Pu debate had all been dismissed, and begged to be demoted with them; he received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission he learned that Lü Hui and the others who had remonstrated against the Pu honors had all been dismissed. He asked to be demoted with them, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 趣入對，英宗曰：「卿欲就龍逢、比干之名，孰若效伊尹、傅說哉？」

translations.literal: He was hurried into audience; Emperor Yingzong said, "Do you wish to win the names of Long Feng and Bi Gan, or would it not be better to emulate Yi Yin and Fu Yue?"
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned back to audience. Emperor Yingzong said, "Do you want the fame of Long Feng and Bi Gan, or would it not be better to serve the throne like Yi Yin and Fu Yue?

sentences.zh: 瞻皇懼，言：「臣不敢奉詔，使朝廷有同罪異罰之譏。」

translations.literal: Zhan was awestruck and afraid, saying, "Your subject dares not accept the edict, lest the court incur the reproach of equal guilt with unequal punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was awestruck and afraid. He said, "I dare not accept that command, lest the court be reproached for punishing the same offense differently.

sentences.zh: 遂通判汾州。

translations.literal: He was then made vice prefect of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made vice prefect of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，遷司封員外郎、知商州，又除提點陝西刑獄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne he was transferred to Assistant in the Ministry of Rites' Enfeoffment Section and made prefect of Shang Prefecture, then appointed Intendant of Shaanxi Judicial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, Zhao was promoted to Assistant in the Ministry of Rites' Enfeoffment Section and made prefect of Shang Prefecture, then appointed Intendant of Shaanxi Judicial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，為開封府判官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining he became an administrative aide of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he became an administrative aide of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神宗問：「卿知青苗法便乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong asked, "Do you know whether the Green Sprouts Law is convenient?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong asked, "Do you think the Green Sprouts Law is convenient?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「青苗法，唐行之於季世擾攘中，掊民財誠便。

translations.literal: He replied, "The Green Sprouts Law—when the Tang applied it in the turmoil of a dynasty's last age, stripping the people's wealth, it was indeed convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Green Sprouts Law was used by the Tang in the turmoil of a dynasty's decline. For stripping the people's wealth, it was indeed convenient.

sentences.zh: 今欲為長久計，愛養百姓，誠不便。」

translations.literal: Now if one wishes to plan for the long term and cherish and nurture the common people, it is truly not convenient."
translations.idiomatic: But if you wish to plan for the long term and cherish the common people, it is truly unsuitable."

sentences.zh: 初，王安石欲瞻助己，使其黨餌以知雜御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning Wang Anshi wished Zhan to assist himself and had his faction bait him with the post of Director of Miscellaneous Censorial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Anshi had wanted Zhao to support him and had his faction offer him the post of miscellaneous censor.

sentences.zh: 瞻不應，由是不得留京師，出為陝西轉運副使，改永興軍轉運使。

translations.literal: Zhan did not respond; thereby he could not remain in the capital, was sent out as Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi Transport, and changed to Commissioner of Yongxing Circuit Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao did not accept. He was therefore unable to remain in the capital and was sent out as Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi Transport, then made Commissioner of Yongxing Circuit Transport.

sentences.zh: 以親老，請知同州。

translations.literal: Because his parents were aged, he requested to be prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his parents' advanced age, he asked to be made prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，朝廷患錢重，議以交子權之，命瞻制置。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the court worried that cash was heavy and discussed using jiaozi to balance it, and ordered Zhan to oversee the arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xining the court worried that copper cash had become too heavy to carry conveniently and discussed using jiaozi notes to offset it, ordering Zhao to oversee the scheme.

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「有本錢足恃，法乃可行，如多出空券，是罔民也。」

translations.literal: Zhan said, "If there is principal capital sufficient to rely on, the law then may be implemented; if many empty notes are issued, it is deceiving the people."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "The measure can work only if there is sufficient reserve capital to back it. Issuing too many empty notes would be deceiving the people."

sentences.zh: 議不合，移京西轉運使；

translations.literal: The discussion did not agree and he was transferred to Commissioner of Jingxi Transport;
translations.idiomatic: His views did not prevail, and he was transferred to Commissioner of Jingxi Transport;

sentences.zh: 又以親老不行，徙陝州，請還鄉里，除提舉鳳翔太平宮。

translations.literal: Again because his parents were aged he did not go, was moved to Shaan Prefecture, requested to return to his home district, and was appointed to oversee Fengxiang's Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Again citing his parents' age he did not take up the post and was moved to Shaan Prefecture. He asked to return home and was appointed commissioner of Fengxiang's Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服除，易朝請大夫、知滄州。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father; when the mourning ended he was changed to Gentleman for Court Appearances and made prefect of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father's death, when the mourning period ended he was promoted to Gentleman for Court Appearances and made prefect of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，轉朝議大夫，召為太常少卿，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne he was transferred to Grandee of Court Discussion, summoned as Vice Minister of Rites, and moved to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Zhao was promoted to Grandee of Court Discussion, summoned as Vice Minister of Rites, and promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，擢樞密直學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou he was advanced to Academician Ex Officio of the Privy Council and given the concurrent duty of signing Privy Council documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanyou (1088) he was promoted to Academician Ex Officio of the Privy Council with concurrent duty as Privy Council signatory.

sentences.zh: 明年，以中大夫同知院事。

translations.literal: The next year, as Grandee of the Palace he served as Vice Director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Vice Director of the Privy Council with the rank of Grandee of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 因進對言：「機政所急，人才而已。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of an audience he said, "What state affairs urgently need is nothing but talent.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said, "What statecraft urgently needs is talent and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 今臣選武臣難遽盡知，請詔諸路安撫、轉運使舉使臣，科別其才，第為三等，籍之以備選注。」

translations.literal: Now when I select military officers it is hard to know them all at once. I request an edict ordering circuit pacification commissioners and transport commissioners to recommend envoys, classify their talents, rank them in three grades, and register them to prepare for appointment selection."
translations.idiomatic: I find it hard to know military officers thoroughly when selecting them myself. I ask that Your Majesty order the circuit pacification and transport commissioners to recommend officers, classify their talents in three grades, and register them for future appointments."

sentences.zh: 初，元豐中，河決小吳，北注界河，東入於海。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the Yuanfeng era, the Yellow River broke through at Xiao Wu, flowed north into the Jie River, and eastward into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yuanfeng era, the Yellow River broke through at Xiao Wu, flowed north into the Jie River, and eastward into the sea.

sentences.zh: 神宗詔，東流故道淤高，理不可回，其勿復塞。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong decreed that the old course of the eastward flow had silted high and by reason could not be reversed; they should not again block it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong decreed that the old eastward course had silted too high to be restored by reason, and ordered that it not be blocked again.

sentences.zh: 乃開大吳以護北都。

translations.literal: Thereupon Great Wu was opened to protect the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wu was therefore opened to protect the Northern Capital (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 至是，都水王令圖請還河故道，下執政議。

translations.literal: At this time the Director of Waters Wang Lingtu requested to return the river to its old course, and it was sent down to the chief ministers for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Director of Waters Wang Lingtu asked to restore the river's old course, and the matter was referred to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「自河決已八年，未有定論。

translations.literal: Zhan said, "Since the river broke through it has been eight years with no settled conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "It has been eight years since the breach and there is still no settled policy.

sentences.zh: 今遽興大役，役夫三十萬，用木二千萬，臣竊憂焉。

translations.literal: Now suddenly to undertake a great project—laborers three hundred thousand, timber twenty million—I privately am worried.
translations.idiomatic: To launch a massive project now would require three hundred thousand laborers and twenty million units of timber. I am deeply concerned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方遣使相視，若以東流未便，宜亟從之；

translations.literal: The court is just now sending envoys to inspect; if the eastward flow is not convenient, it is fitting to follow that quickly;
translations.idiomatic: The court has just sent envoys to inspect the course. If the eastward flow proves unsuitable, we should follow their recommendation promptly;

sentences.zh: 若以為可回，宜為數歲之計，以緩民力」。

translations.literal: if it is thought it can be reversed, it is fitting to make a plan of several years to ease the people's labor."
translations.idiomatic: if restoration is still deemed necessary, we should plan over several years to ease the burden on the people."

sentences.zh: 議者又謂河入界河而北，則失中國之險，昔澶淵之役，非河為限，則北兵不止。

translations.literal: Those in discussion also said that if the river entered the Jie River and flowed north, then China's strategic barrier would be lost; in the past at the Chanyuan campaign, had not the river been the limit, the northern troops would not have stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that if the river entered the Jie River and flowed north, China would lose its strategic barrier. They said that at the Chanyuan campaign, had the river not formed a barrier, the northern troops would not have halted.

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「王者恃德不恃險。

translations.literal: Zhan said, "A true king relies on virtue, not on strategic barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "A true king relies on virtue, not on geographic barriers.

sentences.zh: 昔堯、舜都蒲、冀，周、漢都咸、鎬，皆歷年數百，不聞以河障外國。

translations.literal: In the past Yao and Shun had their capitals at Pu and Ji, Zhou and Han at Xian and Hao—all endured hundreds of years, and one does not hear of using the river to block foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun made their capitals at Pu and Ji; the Zhou and Han at Xian and Hao. Each endured for centuries, and none is said to have relied on a river to hold off foreign states.

sentences.zh: 澶淵之役，蓋廟社之靈，章聖之德，將相之智勇，故敵帥授首，豈獨河之力哉？」

translations.literal: The Chanyuan campaign—was it not the spirit of the ancestral temples, the virtue of Zhang Sheng, the wisdom and courage of generals and ministers that caused the enemy commander to surrender his head? How could it be the power of the river alone?"
