translations.idiomatic: The victory at Chanyuan rested on the spirit of the ancestral temples, the virtue of Emperor Zhenzong, and the wisdom and courage of his generals and ministers. That is why the enemy commander submitted. How could it have been the river's work alone?"

sentences.zh: 後使者以東流非便，水官復請塞北流，瞻固爭之，卒詔罷役，如瞻所議。

translations.literal: Later the envoys reported the eastward flow was not convenient; the water officials again requested to block the northward flow. Zhan firmly contested it, and in the end an edict halted the project, as Zhan had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the envoys reported that the eastward course was unsuitable. The water officials again asked to block the northward flow, but Zhao protested firmly. An edict finally halted the project, as Zhao had urged.

sentences.zh: 洮、河諸族以青唐首領浸弱可制，欲倚中國兵威以廢之，邊臣亟請興師。

translations.literal: The various tribes of Tao and He, seeing the Qingtang leader gradually weakening and controllable, wished to rely on China's military might to abolish him; frontier officials repeatedly requested to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Tao and He, seeing the Qingtang leader grow weak and ripe for control, wished to use Song military might to remove him. Frontier officials repeatedly pressed for war.

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Zhan said, "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "We must not.

sentences.zh: 御外國以大信為本，且既爵命之，彼雖失眾心，無犯王略之罪，何辭而伐之？

translations.literal: Governing foreign states takes great trust as foundation. Moreover, having already enfeoffed and appointed them, though they have lost popular support, they have no crime of violating the royal domain—what pretext to attack them?
translations.idiomatic: In dealing with foreign peoples great faith is the foundation. We have already enfeoffed and appointed them. Though they have lost the hearts of their people, they have not violated imperial territory. What justification is there for attacking them?

sentences.zh: 若其不克，則兵端自此復起矣。」

translations.literal: If they are not overcome, then military troubles from this will rise again."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, war will break out again from this point onward."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 瞻又奏廢渠陽軍，以紓荊湖之力；

translations.literal: Zhan also memorialized to abolish Quchuan Army to ease the strength of Jing and Hu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also memorialized to abolish Quchuan Army to ease the burden on Jing and Hu circuits;

sentences.zh: 乞詔諭西夏使歸永樂遺民，夏人聽命。

translations.literal: He begged an edict instructing Western Xia to return the displaced people of Yongle; the Xia people obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Western Xia be instructed to return the displaced people of Yongle. The Xia complied.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanyou he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后語輔臣曰：「惜哉，忠厚君子也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said to the chief ministers, "What a pity—a loyal and honest gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager told the chief ministers, "What a pity. He was a loyal and honest gentleman."

sentences.zh: 車駕親臨，輟視朝二日。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage personally came; court audiences were suspended for two days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally attended his funeral, and court audiences were suspended for two days.

sentences.zh: 贈銀青光祿大夫，諡曰懿簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Silver Blue-Glitter Grandee of Glorious Blessing; his posthumous title was Yijian (Blessed and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded Silver Blue-Glitter Grandee of Glorious Blessing, with the posthumous title Yijian (Blessed and Simple).

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，言者以傅會元祐諸臣，追奪所贈官，列於黨籍。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng, memorializers said he had curried favor with Yuanyou ministers; his posthumous rank was stripped and he was listed in the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng (1094–1098) critics charged that he had colluded with Yuanyou ministers. His posthumous honors were revoked and he was listed in the faction register.

sentences.zh: 瞻著《春秋論》二十卷，《史記牴牾論》五卷，《唐春秋》五十卷，《奏議》十卷，《文集》二十卷，《西山別錄》一卷。

translations.literal: Zhan authored "Discourses on the Spring and Autumn" in twenty juan, "Discourse on Contradictions in the Records of the Historian" five juan, "Spring and Autumn of Tang" fifty juan, "Memorials" ten juan, "Collected Writings" twenty juan, and "Separate Record of Western Hills" one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao authored Discourses on the Spring and Autumn Annals (20 juan), Discourse on Contradictions in the Records of the Historian (5 juan), Spring and Autumn of Tang (50 juan), Memorials (10 juan), Collected Writings (20 juan), and Separate Record of Western Hills (1 juan).

sentences.zh: 四子：孝諶，瀛州錄事參軍；

translations.literal: Four sons: Xiaochen, Recorder of Ying Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Xiaochen, staff officer of Ying Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 獻誠，唐城令；

translations.literal: Xiancheng, magistrate of Tangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng, magistrate of Tangcheng;

sentences.zh: 某，蚤卒；

translations.literal: Mou, died early;
translations.idiomatic: one [name omitted], who died young;

sentences.zh: 彥詒，太康主簿。

translations.literal: Yanyi, registrar of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: and Yanyi, registrar of Taikang.

sentences.zh: 傅堯俞

translations.literal: Fu Yaoyu
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yaoyu

sentences.zh: 傅堯俞，字欽之，本鄆州須城人，徙孟州濟源。

translations.literal: Fu Yaoyu, style name Qinzhi, was originally from Xucheng in Yan Prefecture and moved to Jiyuan in Meng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yaoyu, whose style name was Qinzhi, was originally from Xucheng in Yan Prefecture and later moved to Jiyuan in Meng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十歲能為文，及登第，猶未冠。

translations.literal: At age ten he could compose prose; when he passed the examination he had still not capped his maturity.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could already compose prose, and when he passed the civil service examination he had not yet come of age.

sentences.zh: 石介每過之，堯俞未嘗不在，介曰：「君少年決科，不以遊戲為娛，何也？」

translations.literal: Whenever Shi Jie visited, Yaoyu was never absent. Jie said, "You are young and have decided on passing the examination—why do you not take games as amusement?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shi Jie visited, Yaoyu was always present. Jie said, "You are young and already set on passing the examinations. Why do you not amuse yourself with games?"

sentences.zh: 堯俞曰：「性不喜囂雜，非有他爾。」

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "By nature I do not like noise and commotion; there is no other reason."
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "By nature I dislike noise and bustle. There is no other reason."

sentences.zh: 介嘆息奇之。

translations.literal: Jie sighed and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sighed and marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 嘗監西京稅院事，留守晏殊、夏竦皆謂曰：「子有清識雅度，文約而理盡，卿相才也。」

translations.literal: He once supervised the Western Capital Tax Office; the prefects Yan Shu and Xia Song both said to him, "You have pure insight and elegant bearing; your writing is concise and the reasoning exhausts the matter—you have the talent of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: When he supervised the Western Capital Tax Office, the prefects Yan Shu and Xia Song both told him, "You have pure insight and elegant bearing. Your writing is concise yet exhaustive in reasoning. You have the talent of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 知新息縣，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Xinxin County and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Xinxin County and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐末，為監察物史。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiayou he became a supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiayou era he became a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 袞國公主下嫁李瑋，為家監梁懷吉、張承照所間，與夫不相中。

translations.literal: The Princess of Guo State married Li Wei; she was alienated by household supervisors Liang Huaiji and Zhang Chengzhao and estranged from her husband.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Guo married Li Wei but was estranged from her husband by her household supervisors Liang Huaiji and Zhang Chengzhao, who came between them.

sentences.zh: 仁宗斥二人於外，未幾，復還主家，出瑋知衛州。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong expelled the two men from court; before long they were returned to the princess's household, and Wei was sent out as prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong expelled the two men from court, but before long they were returned to the princess's household while Wei was sent out to serve as prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 堯俞言：「主恃愛薄其夫，陛下為逐瑋而還隸臣，甚悖禮，為四方笑，後何以誨諸女乎？」

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "The princess relies on favor and slighted her husband. Your Majesty expelled Wei yet returned these subjects to her service—this greatly violates ritual. The realm will laugh. How will you later instruct your daughters?"
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "The princess relies on imperial favor and slighted her husband. Your Majesty expelled Wei yet returned these attendants to her service. This gravely violates ritual propriety and will make the realm laugh. How will you later instruct your other daughters?"

sentences.zh: 皇城邏卒吳清誣奏富民殺人，鞠治無狀，有司須清辨，內侍主者不遣。

translations.literal: A patrolman of the Imperial City Guards, Wu Qing, falsely memorialized that a wealthy man had killed someone. Investigation found no basis. The relevant office required Qing to testify, but the eunuch in charge would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: A patrolman of the Imperial City Guards, Wu Qing, falsely reported that a wealthy man had committed murder. Investigation found no basis for the charge. The relevant office required Qing to testify, but the eunuch in charge would not release him.

sentences.zh: 堯俞言：「陛下惜清，恐不復聞外事矣。

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "Your Majesty cherishes Qing—I fear you will no longer hear of outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "Your Majesty cherishes Qing. I fear you will no longer hear of affairs outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 臣以為不若使付外，暴其是非而行賞罰焉，則事之上聞者皆實，乃所以廣視聽也。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks it would be better to hand the case to the outer bureaucracy, expose right and wrong and impose rewards and punishments—then what reaches Your Majesty will all be true, and that is how to broaden sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I believe it would be better to hand the case to the outer bureaucracy, expose the rights and wrongs, and impose proper rewards and punishments. Then what reaches Your Majesty will all be true, and that is how to broaden your sight and hearing.

sentences.zh: 縱而不問，則讒者肆行，民無所措手足，尚欲求治，得乎？」

translations.literal: If indulged without inquiry, slanderers will run riot and the people will have nowhere to set hand or foot—can you still seek good order?"
translations.idiomatic: If such cases are indulged without inquiry, slanderers will run riot and the people will have nowhere to turn. Can good order still be sought?"

sentences.zh: 內侍李允恭、朱晦屈法任其子，趙繼寵越次管當天章閣，蔡世寧掌內藏，而以珠私示內人。

translations.literal: Eunuchs Li Yun'gong and Zhu Hui bent the law to appoint their sons; Zhao Jibao out of turn managed the Tianzhang Pavilion; Cai Shining managed the inner treasury and privately showed pearls to palace women.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Li Yun'gong and Zhu Hui bent the law to appoint their sons; Zhao Jibao was put in charge of the Tianzhang Pavilion out of turn; Cai Shining managed the inner treasury and privately showed pearls to palace women.

sentences.zh: 堯俞以為嬖寵恩幸過失，當防之於漸，悉劾之。

translations.literal: Yaoyu held that favoritism and indulgence of the intimate were faults that should be guarded against at the outset; he impeached them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu held that indulgence of favorites was a fault that should be checked at the outset. He impeached them all.

sentences.zh: 時乏國用，言利者爭獻富國計。

translations.literal: At the time state revenue was scarce; profit-seekers competed to present plans to enrich the state.
translations.idiomatic: At the time state revenue was scarce, and profit-seekers competed to present plans to enrich the treasury.

sentences.zh: 堯俞奏曰：「今度支歲用不足，誠不可忽，然欲救其弊，在陛下宜自儉刻，身先天下，無奪農時，勿害商旅，如是可矣。

translations.literal: Yaoyu memorialized, "Today the Ministry of Revenue's annual expenditure is insufficient—this truly cannot be neglected. Yet to remedy its ills, Your Majesty should begin with frugality, take the lead for all under Heaven, do not seize farmers' seasons, and do not harm merchants and travelers—thus it may be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu memorialized, "The Ministry of Revenue's annual expenditure is indeed insufficient and cannot be neglected. Yet to remedy this, Your Majesty should begin with frugality, take the lead for all under Heaven, do not seize the farmers' seasons, and do not harm merchants and travelers. That would suffice.

sentences.zh: 不然，徒欲紛更，為之無益，聚斂者用，則天下殆矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, merely wishing to change this and that will do no good; if revenue-raising methods are employed, then the realm will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, merely changing policies back and forth will do no good. If revenue-raising schemes are adopted, the realm will be in peril."

sentences.zh: 仁宗春秋高，皇嗣未立，堯俞請建宗室之賢，以慰天下望。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong's years were advanced and the imperial heir was not yet established. Yaoyu requested to establish a worthy from the imperial clan to satisfy the realm's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was advanced in years and the imperial heir had not yet been named. Yaoyu asked that a worthy member of the imperial clan be established as heir to satisfy the hopes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 及英宗為皇子，有司闕供饋，仁宗未知。

translations.literal: When Yingzong became heir apparent, the relevant office lacked supplies for his sustenance; Renzong did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was made heir apparent, the relevant offices failed to provide adequate supplies, and Renzong did not know.

sentences.zh: 堯俞言：「陛下既以宗社之重建皇嗣，宜以家人禮，使皇子朝夕侍膳左右，以通慈孝之誠。

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "Your Majesty has already reestablished the heir for the altars of soil and grain. You should use family ritual, have the prince attend morning and evening meals at your side, to communicate filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "Your Majesty has already reestablished the heir for the sake of the altars of soil and grain. You should treat him with family ritual, have the prince attend your meals morning and evening, and thereby express the bond of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 今禮遇有闕，非所以隆親親、重國本也。」

translations.literal: Now the ceremonial treatment has gaps—this is not how to exalt kinship and weigh the foundation of the state."
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial treatment he now receives is deficient. That is not how to exalt kinship and strengthen the foundation of the state."

sentences.zh: 於是詔有司供具甚厚。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the relevant office to supply provisions very generously.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the relevant offices to supply provisions very generously.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，轉殿中侍御史，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: When Yingzong took the throne he was transferred to Attendant Censor of the Palace and promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, Yaoyu was transferred to Attendant Censor of the Palace and promoted to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 皇太后與英宗同聽政，英宗有疾，既平，堯俞上書皇太后，請還政。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Yingzong jointly heard government; Yingzong had illness, and when it abated Yaoyu memorialized the Empress Dowager requesting the return of government.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and Yingzong ruled jointly. When Yingzong fell ill and recovered, Yaoyu memorialized the Empress Dowager asking her to return government to him.

sentences.zh: 久之，聞內侍任守忠有讒間語，堯俞諫皇太后曰：「外間物論紛惑，兩宮之情未通。

translations.literal: After a long time he heard the eunuch Ren Shouzhong had slanderous words to sow discord. Yaoyu remonstrated the Empress Dowager, saying, "Outside the court public discussion is in turmoil; the feelings between the two palaces are not yet communicated.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he heard that the eunuch Ren Shouzhong was spreading slander to sow discord. Yaoyu remonstrated with the Empress Dowager, saying, "Public discussion outside the palace is in turmoil, and the feelings between the two palaces are not yet reconciled.

sentences.zh: 臣謂天下之可信者，無大於以天下與人，亦無大於受天下以公，況皇帝以明睿之資，貫通古今，而受人之天下乎？

translations.literal: Your subject says there is nothing greater in credibility under Heaven than giving the realm to another, and nothing greater than receiving the realm with public principle—how much more when the emperor with discerning sagacity comprehends past and present yet receives the realm from people?
translations.idiomatic: I say there is nothing greater in earning trust under Heaven than giving the realm to another, and nothing greater than receiving the realm in the public interest—how much more when the emperor, with discerning sagacity and mastery of past and present, has received the realm from the people?

sentences.zh: 如誅竄讒人，則慈孝之聲並隆矣。」

translations.literal: If slanderers are executed and expelled, then the voice of filial devotion will rise together."
translations.idiomatic: If slanderers are executed and expelled, the renown of filial devotion will rise together."

sentences.zh: 於是皇太后還政，逐守忠。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Empress Dowager returned government and expelled Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Empress Dowager returned government to the emperor and expelled Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 堯俞言於英宗曰：「皇太后給事左右之人，宜頗錄其勤勞，少加恩惠，上慰母后，下安反側。

translations.literal: Yaoyu said to Yingzong, "Those attending the Empress Dowager on her left and right ought to have their labor recorded and be given some favor, to comfort the mother above and settle those below.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said to Yingzong, "Those who attend the Empress Dowager should have their service recorded and be given some favor, to comfort your mother above and settle those below.

sentences.zh: 且守忠已去，其餘不問可也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Shouzhong is already gone; the rest may go uninvestigated."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Shouzhong is already gone. The rest may go uninvestigated."

sentences.zh: 遷右司諫、同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Remonstrance Official and Concurrent Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Remonstrance Official and Concurrent Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 英宗眷遇堯俞，嘗雪中賜對，堯俞自東廡升，英宗傾身東向以待，每奏事退，多目送之。

translations.literal: Yingzong showed special regard for Yaoyu. Once in snow he granted audience; Yaoyu ascended from the east wing corridor and Yingzong bent his body eastward to await him. Each time he finished presenting a matter and withdrew, the emperor often watched him go.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong showed special regard for Yaoyu. Once during a snowfall he granted him audience. Yaoyu ascended from the east wing corridor, and Yingzong bent forward facing east to receive him. Each time Yaoyu finished presenting a matter and withdrew, the emperor often watched him go.

sentences.zh: 嘗問曰：「多士盈庭，孰忠孰邪？」

translations.literal: He once asked, "Many officers fill the hall—which are loyal and which wicked?"
translations.idiomatic: He once asked, "Many officers fill the court. Which are loyal and which are wicked?"

sentences.zh: 堯俞曰：「大忠大佞，固不可移；

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "Great loyalty and great wickedness naturally cannot be shifted;
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "Great loyalty and great wickedness cannot be changed;

sentences.zh: 中人之性，繫上所化。」

translations.literal: the nature of middling men depends on what the sovereign transforms them into."
translations.idiomatic: but middling men depend on how the sovereign shapes them."

sentences.zh: 英宗納其言。

translations.literal: Yingzong accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 時英宗初躬庶政，猶謙讓任大臣，堯俞言：「大臣之言是，陛下偶以為然而行之可也；

translations.literal: At the time Yingzong had first personally attended to ordinary government but still yielded and relied on great ministers. Yaoyu said, "When great ministers' words are right, Your Majesty may happen to agree and carry them out—that is acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yingzong had first begun to attend to government personally but still deferred to his great ministers. Yaoyu said, "When a great minister's words are right, Your Majesty may happen to agree and carry them out—that is acceptable;

sentences.zh: 審其非矣，從而徇之，則人主之柄安在？

translations.literal: but if you examine and find they are wrong, yet follow and indulge them—where then does the sovereign's handle lie?
translations.idiomatic: but if you examine them and find they are wrong, yet follow and indulge them—where then does the sovereign's authority lie?

sentences.zh: 願君臣之際，是是非非，毋相面從。

translations.literal: I wish that between ruler and minister right and wrong may be clear and that none face each other with mere compliance.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that between ruler and minister right and wrong may be clear, and that none merely comply to each other's face.

sentences.zh: 總覽眾議，無所適莫，則威柄歸陛下矣。」

translations.literal: Take comprehensive view of all opinions, follow none exclusively or reject none absolutely—then authority will return to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Take comprehensive account of all opinions, favoring none exclusively, and authority will return to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 嘗因論事，英宗曰：「卿何不言蔡襄？」

translations.literal: Once in discussing affairs Yingzong said, "Why do you not speak of Cai Xiang?"
translations.idiomatic: Once during a discussion of state affairs Yingzong said, "Why do you not speak against Cai Xiang?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若襄有罪，何不自正典刑，安用臣言？」

translations.literal: He replied, "If Xiang is guilty, why not yourself apply the proper punishment—why use my words?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If Xiang is guilty, why not apply the proper punishment yourself? Why use my words?"

sentences.zh: 英宗曰：「欲使台諫言，以公議出之。」

translations.literal: Yingzong said, "I wish to have the censorate and remonstrance officers speak, bringing it forth through public discussion."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong said, "I wish the censorate and remonstrance officers to speak, bringing the matter forth through public discussion."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「若付之公議，臣但見襄辦山陵事有功，不見其罪。

translations.literal: He replied, "If entrusted to public discussion, your subject only sees Xiang's merit in managing the imperial tomb works—your subject does not see his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If entrusted to public discussion, I only see Xiang's merit in managing the imperial tomb works. I do not see his crime.

sentences.zh: 臣身為諫官，使臣受旨言事，臣不敢。」

translations.literal: Your subject serves as remonstrance official; to have your subject receive an edict to speak on a matter—your subject dares not."
translations.idiomatic: As a remonstrance official, to have me receive an edict to speak on a matter—I dare not."

sentences.zh: 陝西言，近邊熟戶頗逃失。

translations.literal: Shaanxi reported that recently border assimilated households had largely fled and been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi reported that many assimilated border households had recently fled or been lost.

sentences.zh: 詔以內侍李若愚等為陝西四路鈐轄，專使招納，歲一入奏事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed eunuchs Li Ruoyu and others as Supervisory Commissioners of the four Shaanxi circuits, specially to recruit and entice them; each year once they entered to report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed the eunuchs Li Ruoyu and others as supervisory commissioners of the four Shaanxi circuits, charged specifically with recruiting them, with annual reports to the throne.

sentences.zh: 堯俞言：「此安撫、經略使職也。

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "This is the duty of pacification and frontier commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "This is the duty of pacification and frontier commissioners.

sentences.zh: 且若愚等，陛下不信其言，則如不用；

translations.literal: Moreover as for Ruoyu and the rest—if Your Majesty does not trust their words, it is as if not using them;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if Your Majesty does not trust their words, it is as if you do not use them at all;

sentences.zh: 言必見從，則邊帥之權，移於四人矣。」

translations.literal: if their words are certainly followed, then the frontier commanders' authority shifts to these four men."
translations.idiomatic: but if their words are always followed, the authority of the frontier commanders will shift to these four men."

sentences.zh: 尋罷之。

translations.literal: Soon it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 大臣建言濮安懿王宜稱皇考，堯俞曰：「此於人情禮文，皆大謬戾。」

translations.literal: Great ministers proposed that Prince Pu Anyi should be styled Imperial Father. Yaoyu said, "In human sentiment and ritual text this is all greatly erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers proposed that Prince Pu Anyi should be styled Imperial Father. Yaoyu said, "In human sentiment and ritual propriety this is gravely mistaken.

sentences.zh: 與侍御史呂誨同上十余疏，其言極功。

translations.literal: Together with Attending Censorial Investigator Lü Hui he jointly submitted more than ten memorials; their words were extremely forceful.
translations.idiomatic: He and the investigating censor Lü Hui submitted more than ten joint memorials, pressing their arguments to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 主議者知恟々不可遏，遂易「考」稱「親」。

translations.literal: Those who led the policy knew the clamor could not be checked, and therefore changed "Father" to "Kin."
translations.idiomatic: The proponents saw the uproar could not be stemmed and substituted the title Imperial Father (kao) with Imperial Kin (qin).

sentences.zh: 堯俞又言：「『親』，非父母而何？

translations.literal: Yaoyu said again, "'Kin'—if not father and mother, then what?
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu spoke again: "'Kin'—if it does not mean father and mother, what does it mean?

sentences.zh: 亦不可也。

translations.literal: That too is not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: That too is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 夫恩義存亡一也，先帝既以陛下為子，當是時，設濮王尚無恙，陛下得以父名之乎？」

translations.literal: Favor and obligation are one whether in life or death. The late emperor already took Your Majesty as son—at that time, had Prince Pu still been well, could Your Majesty have named him father?"
translations.idiomatic: Favor and obligation are the same in life and in death. The late emperor had already taken Your Majesty as his son—at that moment, if Prince Pu had still been alive and well, could Your Majesty have addressed him as father?"

sentences.zh: 又因水災言：「簡宗廟，則水不潤下。

translations.literal: He also spoke because of flood disasters: "If ancestral temples are reduced, water will not soak downward.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke in connection with the floods: "When ancestral temples are curtailed, water does not soak the earth below.

sentences.zh: 今以濮王為皇考，於仁宗之廟，簡孰甚焉。」

translations.literal: Now to take Prince Pu as Imperial Father—in Renzong's temple, what reduction could be greater?"
translations.idiomatic: To make Prince Pu Imperial Father now—what greater curtailment could there be to Renzong's temple?"

sentences.zh: 俄命堯俞與趙瞻使契丹，比還，呂誨、呂大防、范純仁皆以諫濮議罷，復除堯俞侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Soon Yaoyu and Zhao Zhan were ordered as envoys to Khitan. When they returned, Lü Hui, Lü Daguan, and Fan Chunren were all dismissed for remonstrating on the Pu affair; Yaoyu was again appointed Attending Censor with concurrent miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yaoyu and Zhao Zhan were dispatched as envoys to the Khitan. After they returned, Lü Hui, Lü Daguan, and Fan Chunren were all removed for opposing the Pu affair; Yaoyu was reappointed Attending Censor with concurrent charge of miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 堯俞拜疏必求罷去，英宗面留之。

translations.literal: Yaoyu submitted memorials bowing and begging to resign; Yingzong detained him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu repeatedly submitted memorials asking to be dismissed; Yingzong kept him in person.

sentences.zh: 堯俞言：「誨等已逐，臣義不當止。」

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "Hui and the others have already been expelled; in righteousness your servant ought not stop."
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "Hui and the others have already been driven out; in duty I ought not remain."

sentences.zh: 因再拜辭，英宗愕然，曰：「是果不可留也。」

translations.literal: He bowed twice and took leave. Yingzong was startled and said, "This one truly cannot be kept."
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and withdrew. Yingzong was taken aback and said, "This man truly cannot be kept."

sentences.zh: 遂出知和州。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out to serve as prefect of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 通判楊洙乘間問曰：「公以直言斥居此，何為未嘗言及御史時事？」

translations.literal: Vice-Prefect Yang Zhu, seizing an interval, asked, "You were sent here for blunt speech—why have you never spoken of censorial affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Prefect Yang Zhu took an opportune moment to ask, "You were banished here for speaking plainly—why have you never mentioned affairs from your days as censor?"

sentences.zh: 堯俞曰：「前日言職也，豈得已哉？

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "That was the duty of speech—how could one stop?
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "That was the office of remonstrance—how could one have held back?

sentences.zh: 今日為郡守，當宣朝廷美意，而反呫呫追言前日之闕政，與誹謗何異？」

translations.literal: Today as prefect one should proclaim the court's good intent; to mutter on and on about yesterday's governmental faults—how is that different from slander?"
translations.idiomatic: Today as a prefect one should proclaim the court's good intent; to keep muttering over yesterday's governmental lapses—how is that different from slander?"

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，徙知廬州。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, he was transferred to prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong acceded, Yaoyu was transferred to prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，至京師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 王安石素與之善，方行新法，謂之曰：「舉朝紛紛，俟尹來久矣，將以待制、諫院處君。」

translations.literal: Wang Anshi had long been on good terms with him and was then implementing the New Policies. He said to him, "The whole court is in turmoil; we have long awaited your coming—intending to place you as preparing draftsman in the Remonstrance Bureau."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had long been friendly with him and was then enacting the New Policies. He told him, "The whole court is in an uproar; we have long awaited your arrival—and intend to place you as a drafting academician in the Remonstrance Bureau."

sentences.zh: 堯俞曰：「新法世以為不便，誠如是，當極論之。

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "The world considers the New Policies inconvenient; if it is truly so, one ought to argue it to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "The world considers the New Policies ill-suited; if that is truly so, I shall argue the point to the full.

sentences.zh: 平生未嘗好欺，敢以為告。」

translations.literal: All my life I have never liked deception—I venture to tell you this."
translations.idiomatic: I have never in my life been fond of deceit, and I venture to tell you so plainly."

sentences.zh: 安石慍之，但授直昭文館、權鹽鐵副仗，俄出為河北轉運使，改知江寧府。

translations.literal: Anshi was angered and only appointed him Direct Attendant of the Zhaowen Pavilion and Acting Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron; soon he was sent out as Hebei transport commissioner, then changed to prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi took offense and merely gave him Direct Attendant of the Zhaowen Pavilion and acting Vice Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission; soon he was sent out as Hebei transport commissioner, then reassigned as prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，言：「仁廟一室，與藝祖、太宗併為百代不遷之主。」

translations.literal: On farewell audience at court he said, "Renzong's single hall, together with Taizu and Taizong, are undying sovereigns for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he said, "Renzong's single shrine, together with Taizu and Taizong, are undying sovereigns for a hundred generations."

sentences.zh: 徙許州、河陽、徐州，再歲六移官，困於道路，知不為時所容，請提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: He was shifted to Xu Prefecture, Heyang, and Xu Prefecture; in two years six transfers of office, wearied on the roads, knowing he was not tolerated by the times, he requested to superintend Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved through Xu Prefecture, Heyang, and Xuzhou; within two years he changed posts six times, worn out on the road, and seeing that the age would not accommodate him, he asked to superintend Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 先是，徐人告有談天文休咎者，堯俞以事未白，不受辭。

translations.literal: Earlier, a man of Xu reported someone discussing astronomy and good and ill fortune; Yaoyu, because the matter was not yet clarified, did not accept the complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, someone in Xuzhou reported a person who spoke of celestial signs and fortune and misfortune; Yaoyu, because the case was not yet clear, declined to take the accusation.

sentences.zh: 談者後伏誅，堯俞坐不即捕，削官職。

translations.literal: The talker was later executed; Yaoyu was punished for not immediately arresting him and his office titles were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: The speaker was later executed; Yaoyu was punished for failing to arrest him at once and was stripped of his ranks.

sentences.zh: 稍起，監黎陽縣倉草場，郡掾行縣，堯俞從眾出迎盡禮。

translations.literal: He was slightly raised to supervise the Liyang County granary hay yard; when a prefectural clerk toured the county, Yaoyu went out with the crowd to welcome him with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually restored to supervise the Liyang County granary hay depot; when a prefectural clerk made a circuit of the county, Yaoyu went out with the others to receive him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 守為遣他吏代主出納，堯俞不可，曰：「居其官安得曠其職。」

translations.literal: The prefect wished to send another clerk to replace him in receipts and disbursements; Yaoyu would not agree and said, "Occupying the office—how can one neglect the duty?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect wanted to send another clerk to handle receipts and disbursements in his stead; Yaoyu refused, saying, "While one holds the post, how can one neglect the charge?"

sentences.zh: 雖寒暑，必日至庾中治事，凡十年。

translations.literal: Though cold or heat, he had to arrive daily at the granary to handle affairs—for ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In cold or heat alike he came every day to the granary to conduct business—for ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，自知明州召為秘書少監兼侍講，擢給事中、吏部侍郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Zhezong took the throne, from his post as prefect of Ming Prefecture he was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Court Lecturer, then promoted to Supervising Censor, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong acceded, he was summoned from Ming Prefecture as Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Court Lecturer, then promoted through Supervising Censor, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「人才有能有不能，如使臣補闕拾遺以輔盛德，明善正失以平庶政，舉直措枉以正大臣，臣雖不才，敢不儘力。

translations.literal: He memorialized, "Talents have what they can and cannot do. If you employ your servant to fill gaps and recover oversights to assist your abundant virtue, clarify good and correct errors to level common government, and promote the upright and set aside the crooked to rectify great ministers—though your servant lacks talent, how dare he not exhaust his strength?
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Talents differ in what they can and cannot do. If Your Majesty would have me fill gaps and recover oversights to support your abundant virtue, clarify what is good and correct what is wrong to steady ordinary government, and promote the upright while setting aside the crooked to rectify great ministers—though I lack ability, how could I not give my utmost?

sentences.zh: 若使窺人陰私，抉人細故，則非臣所能，亦非臣之志也。」

translations.literal: If you make one spy on people's hidden privacies and pick out people's minute faults, that is not what your servant can do, nor is it your servant's aim."
translations.idiomatic: But if you would have me pry into private lives and pick at petty faults, that is neither within my power nor in keeping with my intent."

sentences.zh: 御史張舜民以言事罷，詔堯俞更舉御史，堯俞封還詔書，請留舜民。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Shunmin was dismissed for speaking on affairs; an edict ordered Yaoyu to nominate another censor. Yaoyu sealed and returned the edict, asking to retain Shunmin.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Zhang Shunmin was dismissed for remonstrating, the court ordered Yaoyu to nominate a replacement; Yaoyu sealed the edict and returned it, asking that Shunmin be kept.

sentences.zh: 不聽，即以堯俞為吏部侍郎，堯俞不可，遂以龍圖閣待制知陳州。

translations.literal: They did not listen and immediately made Yaoyu Vice Minister of Personnel; Yaoyu would not accept, and he was then made Dragon Diagram Hall Academician in Waiting and prefect of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not agree and at once appointed Yaoyu Vice Minister of Personnel; he declined, and was therefore made a Dragon Diagram Hall academician in waiting and prefect of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為吏部侍郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was again Vice Minister of Personnel and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again Vice Minister of Personnel and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 前宰相蔡確坐詩誹謗，貶新州，宰執、侍從以下，罷者七八人，御史府為之一空。

translations.literal: Former Chief Councillor Cai Que sat in guilt for poetic slander and was demoted to Xin Prefecture; among chief administrators, attendants, and those below, seven or eight were dismissed, and the Censorate was emptied for it.
translations.idiomatic: Former chief councillor Cai Que was convicted of slander in verse and demoted to Xin Prefecture; among chief administrators, attendants, and those below, seven or eight were removed, and the Censorate was left nearly empty.

sentences.zh: 堯俞曰：「確之黨，其尤者固宜逐，其餘可以一切置之。」

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "Of Que's faction, the worst certainly ought to be expelled; the rest may all be set aside at once."
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "Among Que's faction, the worst offenders should indeed be driven out; the rest may be set aside entirely."

sentences.zh: 且言：「以陛下盛德，而乃於此不能平？

translations.literal: He also said, "With Your Majesty's abundant virtue, and yet on this you cannot be at peace?
translations.idiomatic: He added, "With Your Majesty's abundant virtue, can you not be tranquil even here?

sentences.zh: 願聽之如蚊虻之過耳，無使有纖微之忤，以奸太和之氣。

translations.literal: I wish you would hear it as mosquitoes and gadflies pass the ear, and not let the slightest offense harm the great harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty hear such things as mosquitoes and gnats pass the ear, and not let the slightest affront disturb the great harmonious breath of the realm.

sentences.zh: 事至，以無心應之，聖人所以養至誠而御遐福也。」

translations.literal: When affairs arrive, respond with no mind—that is how the sage nourishes utmost sincerity and receives distant blessing."
translations.idiomatic: When matters arise, meet them with an unperturbed mind—that is how the sage cultivates utmost sincerity and secures blessings from afar."

sentences.zh: 水官李偉議大河可從孫村導之還故道。

translations.literal: Hydraulic official Li Wei proposed that the Great River could be led from Sun Village back to its old course.
translations.idiomatic: Hydraulic official Li Wei proposed that the Yellow River could be diverted from Sun Village back to its former channel.

sentences.zh: 堯俞言：「河事雖不可隃度，然比遣使按之，皆言非便。

translations.literal: Yaoyu said, "River affairs, though they cannot be gauged from afar, yet when envoys were lately sent to inspect, all said it was not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu said, "River works cannot be judged from a distance, yet the envoys recently sent to inspect all reported that the plan was impracticable.

sentences.zh: 而偉又繆悠不肯任責，豈可以遽興大役。」

translations.literal: Moreover Wei is irresponsibly vague and unwilling to bear responsibility—how can one hastily undertake a great labor?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wei is feckless and unwilling to accept responsibility—how can we rush into a major project?"

sentences.zh: 朝廷遂置偉議。

translations.literal: The court then set aside Wei's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon shelved Wei's proposal.

sentences.zh: 進吏部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Personnel with concurrent Court Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel with concurrent Court Reader.

sentences.zh: 元祐四年，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyou he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanyou he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 哲宗與太皇太后哭臨之，太皇太后語輔臣曰：「傅侍郎清直一節，終始不變，金玉君子也。

translations.literal: Zhezong and the Grand Empress Dowager came to weep over him. The Grand Empress Dowager told assisting ministers, "Vice Minister Fu's purity and uprightness in one constant strand never changed from beginning to end—a jade-and-metal gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong and the Grand Empress Dowager came to mourn him. The Grand Empress Dowager told the chief ministers, "Vice Minister Fu was pure and upright in a single unbroken strand from first to last—a gentleman of jade and gold.

sentences.zh: 方倚以相，遽至是乎！」

translations.literal: I had just been relying on him as chief councillor—suddenly to come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: I had only just been relying on him as chief councillor—and suddenly it comes to this!"

sentences.zh: 贈銀青光祿大夫，諡曰獻簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Silver-Gleam Grandee of Glorious Blessing; his posthumous title was Xianjian (Presenting Simplicity).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Silver-Gleam Grandee of Glorious Blessing, with the posthumous title Xianjian (Presenting Simplicity).

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，以元祐黨人，奪贈諡，著名黨籍。

translations.literal: In Shaosheng, as a Yuanyou faction man, his posthumous gifts and title were stripped and his name was entered in the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng, as a Yuanyou partisan, his posthumous honors and title were revoked and his name was entered on the faction roll.

sentences.zh: 後黨錮解，下詔褒贈，錄其子。

translations.literal: Later, when the faction ban was lifted, an edict praised and restored his gifts, and his son was enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the faction proscription was lifted, an edict commended and restored his honors, and his son was enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 堯俞厚重言寡，遇人不設城府，人自不忍欺。

translations.literal: Yaoyu was weighty and spoke little; toward others he set up no inner ramparts, and people themselves could not bear to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoyu was grave and sparing of words; he laid no hidden schemes against others, and people themselves could not bring themselves to cheat him.

sentences.zh: 論事君前，略無回隱，退與人言，不復有矜異色。

translations.literal: When discussing affairs before the ruler he had almost no evasion or concealment; after retiring, in speaking with others, he no longer had a proud, different countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When he argued policy before the throne he scarcely hedged or concealed anything; once he withdrew and spoke with others, he showed no air of special pride.

sentences.zh: 初，自諫官補郡，眾疑法令有未安者，必有所不從，堯俞一切遵之，曰：「君子素其位而行，諫官有言責也，為郡知守法而已。」

translations.literal: At first, when he moved from remonstrance official to fill a prefecture, the crowd suspected that where statutes were not yet settled he would certainly have something he would not follow; Yaoyu followed everything and said, "The gentleman acts according to his position. The remonstrance official has the duty of speech; as prefect one knows only to keep the law."
translations.idiomatic: When he first left the remonstrance bureau for a prefectural post, many expected that wherever the laws seemed unsettled he would refuse to comply; Yaoyu followed them in full and said, "The gentleman acts according to his station. A remonstrance official bears the duty to speak; as a prefect one need only uphold the law."

sentences.zh: 徐前守侵用公錢，堯俞至，為償之，未足而去。

translations.literal: The previous prefect of Xu had embezzled public money; when Yaoyu arrived he repaid it, but before it was fully covered he left.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect of Xuzhou had misappropriated public funds; when Yaoyu arrived he repaid the debt, but left before the sum was fully made up.

sentences.zh: 後守移文堯俞使償入之，考實非堯俞所用，卒不辯。

translations.literal: The later prefect sent a document ordering Yaoyu to repay what had been entered; investigation showed it was not money Yaoyu had used, yet in the end he did not argue.
translations.idiomatic: The succeeding prefect sent papers demanding that Yaoyu make good the shortfall; investigation showed the funds were not his, yet he never defended himself.

sentences.zh: 司馬光嘗謂河南邵雍曰：「清、直、勇之德，人所難兼，吾於欽之見焉。」

translations.literal: Sima Guang once said to Shao Yong of Henan, "The virtues of purity, uprightness, and courage are what people find hard to combine together—I see them in Qin-zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang once said to Shao Yong of Henan, "Purity, uprightness, and courage are virtues men seldom combine—I see all three in Qin-zhi."

sentences.zh: 雍曰：「欽之清而不耀，直而不激，勇而能溫，是為難爾。」

translations.literal: Yong said, "Qin-zhi's purity without dazzling, uprightness without incitement, courage that can yet be warm—that is what is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Qin-zhi is pure without ostentation, upright without harshness, brave yet still gentle—that is what is truly rare."

sentences.zh: 從孫察，見《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: His collateral grandson Cha is seen in the "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: His collateral grandson Fu Cha is treated in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 論曰：存、固、瞻、堯俞，初皆善王安石；

translations.literal: The judgment says: Cun, Gu, Zhan, and Yaoyu were all at first on good terms with Wang Anshi;
translations.idiomatic: The historians' judgment runs: Wang Cun, Sun Gu, Zhao Zhan, and Fu Yaoyu were all initially friendly with Wang Anshi;

sentences.zh: 及其秉政，未嘗受所誘餌，與論新法，終不詭隨。

translations.literal: when he held power they never accepted his bait, and in debating the New Policies they never followed with unprincipled compliance to the end.
translations.idiomatic: yet once he held power they never took his inducements, and in debating the New Policies they never ended in unprincipled acquiescence.

sentences.zh: 及元祐區別正邪，其論蔡確詩謗之罪恐為已甚，將啟朋黨之禍，豈非先知之明乎？

translations.literal: When Yuanyou distinguished orthodox from heterodox, their discussion that Cai Que's crime of poetic slander might be excessive feared opening the calamity of faction—was that not the clarity of foreknowledge?
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanyou drew lines between the righteous and the wicked, their view that the punishment of Cai Que for slander in verse had perhaps gone too far—and would open the door to factional disaster—was that not foresight?

sentences.zh: 他有更張，隨事諫止，不少循默。

translations.literal: On other changes and expansions they remonstrated and stopped matters as they arose, not slightly following in silence.
translations.idiomatic: On other reforms they remonstrated case by case and did not quietly go along.

sentences.zh: 然無矯枉過中之失，故能不亟不徐，進退有道，在元祐諸臣中，身名俱全，亦難矣哉。

translations.literal: Yet they had no fault of overcorrecting the crooked, and therefore could be neither hurried nor slow; in advance and retreat they had the Way. Among the Yuanyou ministers, to have body and name both complete is also hard indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Yet they never overcorrected, and so could move neither too fast nor too slow; in advance and retreat they kept to the proper path. Among the Yuanyou ministers, to preserve both life and reputation intact was no small achievement.
